proposals.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” while I’m looking at a private webpage, remember exactly what I was looking at and why, then bring it back to me on the pendant or Mac when it becomes relevant—without making me find the page again.
proposals.why_useful: Today a logged-in page is stranded in a browser tab: the pendant cannot know which tab the owner means, and a later session has no reliable snapshot of the state or intent. This would turn fleeting authenticated context into a durable, searchable handoff across the browser, Mac, relay, and pendant—useful for invoices, support cases, travel pages, and research that must be resumed later.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to resolve the owner’s short voice instruction and confirm the target tab; use a cheaper background model to title, summarize, extract entities, and rank when to resurface it. The browser extension supplies page evidence; the Mac adds local context only when explicitly relevant.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the save in under 2 seconds; capture and durable storage within 10 seconds. Resurfacing can be scheduled/background and should not consume realtime inference until the owner asks for it.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per saved capsule depending on page length and background summarization; dominant costs are model tokens for normalization and encrypted storage/egress, not browser actions.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page text, URLs, and screenshots leave Safari and are sensitive. Encrypt capsules at rest, retain only the selected extraction plus a short-lived evidence artifact, show source URL/tab/time on every resurfacing, and provide one-tap deletion. Never infer or transmit page content to public relay browsing; the relay should carry encrypted metadata or an owner-requested summary. Saving is reversible, but any follow-up click, form fill, message, purchase, or submission remains a separate action.

For a high-impact action, surface the selected account and evidence in the existing review/receipt record; do not silently switch accounts.

proposals.user_asks: “Pause this browser task and let me resume it later—even if I close Safari.”

On resume it restores the URL/tab, verifies the page fingerprint, re-fills only the reversible staged fields, and presents the exact pending action instead of losing work or submitting anything.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short pause/resume voice exchange; use a cheaper background model to normalize page state, redact secrets, compare fingerprints, and generate the resume summary.

proposals.security_concerns: Page text, URLs, and staged form values may contain private data. Keep the full bundle encrypted on the Mac, store only an opaque task id plus expiry/status on the relay, and never send passwords, cookies, or payment secrets to the model. Resume must stop before irreversible submit/send/purchase and show before/after values and the target URL. Expire and delete bundles on request.

proposals.user_asks: Read this logged-in webpage and answer my question, but keep the private page contents on my Mac; send only the minimum redacted facts and citations needed for the answer to the relay and pendant.

The Mac/browser can inspect the owner's private session, extract only the relevant fields, redact names, tokens, account numbers, and unrelated text locally, then the relay can produce a concise spoken answer with a source URL and timestamp. It works across the browser, Mac, always-awake relay, and pendant, while preserving the owner's existing Safari login and materially reducing exposure.

This would turn a private browser session into a deliberately scoped, expiring handoff that remains useful while walking or away from the desk, without creating a permanent archive of the whole account.
