A pendant alert delivery path using offline_alert_inbox

changes.change: Add a source-integrity witness to every browser finding: record host, canonical URL, capture time, normalized claim hash, and a small structural locator (heading/label path and surrounding character offsets), then provide a read-only recheck job that revisits the page and reports unchanged, changed, or no-longer-found. Keep the current rule of never storing HTML, page text, or screenshots.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the system tells the owner “your account says X,” he can ask whether that exact claim is still true instead of trusting a stale summary. It catches silent edits and expired offers while retaining an auditable pointer to the authenticated source without leaking the page into memory.
changes.effort: Medium: canonicalization and locator extraction in the browser harness, a recheck endpoint, and result mapping into existing provenance. Test against dynamic pages and localization.
changes.risk: DOM redesigns may yield false “not found”; recover by reporting uncertainty and linking the original URL rather than asserting a change. Never treat a hash mismatch alone as fraud or trigger an external action.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage increase per finding (well under 1 KB); one cheap background browser visit per recheck. No meaningful model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Initial capture unchanged; recheck adds one browser round trip, typically 2–10 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves integrity without retaining page content. Canonical URLs and locators can still reveal which origin was used, so protect them under existing provenance access and owner-configured origin policy.
depends_on: Existing POST /memory/browser-findings retention path
Existing GET /browser/provenance and POST /browser/provenance/trace
A stable browser extraction result containing title, URL, and bounded text spans

changes.change: Add an owner-facing browser-memory ledger with two operations: ‘show me every active claim learned from Safari’ and ‘forget this claim/source now.’ The ledger should list host, URL, capture time, expiry, and the downstream brief/alert references, then revoke the selected finding and prevent it from being projected into future prompts. Do not expose or reconstruct the original page text.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can see exactly what the system learned from authenticated browsing and erase a mistaken or sensitive claim immediately. Today provenance can explain where browser-derived information came from, but the owner lacks a simple, end-to-end way to revoke one claim and its downstream use from the pendant or Mac.
changes.effort: Medium: add finding-level identifiers and revocation state to browser memory, a projection filter, a small ledger endpoint/UI, and a pendant-friendly confirmation response.
changes.risk: Revoking a claim could make an existing brief appear incomplete; mark dependent outputs stale and explain why rather than silently deleting their history. Keep an append-only audit of the revocation event without retaining the claim value.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and model cost; one small lookup per prompt projection.
changes.latency_impact: Under 200 ms for listing or revoking local findings; no impact on normal browser reads.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy and user control. The ledger itself must redact values according to the existing browser retention policy and require authenticated owner access.
depends_on: Existing POST /memory/browser-findings
Existing GET /memory/projection
Existing GET /browser/provenance
Existing POST /browser/provenance/trace

changes.change: Add a live-tab lease and explicit handoff marker: when a voice task starts, capture tabId/windowId/url/title plus a content hash; every subsequent browser action must verify the same tab (or return a compact “Safari moved to X” event). Expose “this is the tab I mean” as a one-click/voice handoff and let the owner pin a session until the task ends.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop getting answers about the wrong Safari tab when another app or tab changes focus. Long browser tasks become dependable instead of silently reading a different authenticated page.
changes.effort: Medium: extend browser session state, add hash/identity checks to the existing execute bridge, and surface a handoff event to relay and pendant.
changes.risk: A legitimate navigation changes URL/content and could look like drift; recover by treating same tabId/windowId as authoritative, asking only when the tab identity changes, and allowing an explicit rebind. No page content needs to be persisted.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and compute; one hash per read/action, no additional model call.
changes.latency_impact: Under 50 ms local verification per action; avoids expensive retries and wrong-page model calls.
changes.security_impact: Improves containment of authenticated data by preventing accidental cross-tab reads. Store only tab identity and content hash, not page text.
depends_on: A functioning browser-current-page context action for voice tasks
Existing GET /browser/sessions and POST /execute session plumbing
An owner-visible session pin/handoff control

changes.change: Add a Safari extension “send selection to pendant” command: capture the user-highlighted text plus page title, URL, tab ID, and a short-lived page revision; push it to the relay as an ephemeral context capsule, then let the owner ask a follow-up by voice. The extension must expose explicit selection-only mode separately from whole-page reads and clear the capsule after the interaction.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can highlight one confusing paragraph, press the pendant button, and ask “what does this mean?” without copying or exposing the rest of a private page. It makes precise help possible on pages that are too sensitive or too large to read wholesale.
changes.effort: Medium: Safari extension content-script selection capture, relay context binding, pendant request correlation, and a small UI/voice intent path.
changes.risk: Selection may include secrets or accidental adjacent text; show the captured character count/title before sending when possible, cap size, expire quickly, and provide cancel. If relay delivery fails, the selection stays local and is discarded.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring API cost because context is bounded; roughly 1–3 engineering weeks, no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Selection upload under 1 second; answer latency follows ordinary realtime summarization, typically 2–6 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves least-privilege relative to whole-page capture, but introduces a deliberate data-export action. No HTML/screenshot persistence; URL and bounded selection use existing provenance/TTL rules.
depends_on: A resolved browser action or extension event for selection capture
A session-scoped ephemeral context capsule in relay-realtime
An owner-visible per-origin configuration that can disable selection export

changes.change: Make every browser action carry an immutable tabId and verify the extension result’s tabId, URL, and title against it before returning success; if they differ, fail closed with the requested and observed tab identities and do not create a memory finding. Add a recovery option that re-lists tabs and asks the planner to choose, rather than silently using the active tab.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a request aimed at one tab can return content from another: a live read addressed tab 3658596 but the result contained the active ChatGPT tab 3709209. Without this guard, the assistant could summarize or fill the wrong logged-in page while claiming success.
changes.effort: Medium: propagate tabId through browserBridge/browserPage and extension result validation; add mismatch receipts and planner recovery.
changes.risk: Some existing commands omit tabId and would need explicit default semantics; recovery may add one round trip. Roll back by warning-only logging if extension versions cannot echo identity.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a failed/mismatched command costs one extra browser round trip.
changes.latency_impact: ~0.1–0.5 s verification; mismatch recovery adds 1–3 s.
changes.security_impact: Strongly positive: prevents cross-tab data confusion and wrong-origin mutations. Do not persist mismatch content.
depends_on: Safari extension must echo the requested tabId/windowId in every browser result
POST /execute receipt schema must expose requested vs observed identity

changes.change: Add a read-only browser_context action that asks the Safari extension for the active tab's tabId, origin/title, focused element metadata, selected text, and a bounded DOM snapshot in one response. Include a per-request content budget, explicit source kind (selection/focus/page), and a disposable context ID that later browser_read_page or browser_click calls must reference.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “this page” and get an answer about the exact private page or form field in front of him, instead of the agent guessing among tabs or requiring him to paste sensitive text. It also makes read-only browser work fast and auditable.
changes.effort: Medium: extension content-script capture plus one local-agent bridge action, schema validation, and Safari permission testing. Add redaction and truncation tests for passwords, payment fields, and large pages.
changes.risk: Focused fields may contain secrets or the wrong tab may be captured. Default to selected text/labels, omit input values marked password/payment, show origin and source kind before synthesis, cap payloads, and discard the context after the request. Recovery is simply a new capture; no page mutation occurs.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost beyond one small extraction request; engineering effort is the cost. No hardware change.
changes.latency_impact: Removes a round trip between list-tabs, choose-tab, and read-page; target under 500 ms for metadata and under 2 seconds for a bounded snapshot.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making the capture scope explicit and bounded, but introduces a new sensitive-data boundary. Enforce origin in the returned context and apply existing redaction before relay transmission.
depends_on: A working browser_* dispatch through POST /execute
Safari extension support for active-tab and selection capture
Empty owner-supplied origin policy remaining the authority for whether context may leave the Mac
A relay prompt contract that treats context IDs as disposable evidence, not memory

changes.change: Add a single deterministic browser command `browser_extract_region` that accepts tabId plus a CSS selector or the current selection, returns normalized text, heading, URL, and bounded character count, and expires the result after the requesting job. Keep it read-only and make the command receipt include the selector and timestamp.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask about the exact paragraph, checkout section, or authenticated dashboard card in front of them instead of exposing an entire private page or manually copying it. It is the missing precision primitive behind contradiction checks and safe preflight audits.
changes.effort: Medium: extension content-script selection/selector capture, bridge schema, bounded result handling, and tests on Safari pages with shadow DOM and iframes.
changes.risk: Selectors can be stale or capture the wrong region; return a confidence/empty result and never silently widen to the whole page. Recovery is simply retrying with a new selection; no page mutation occurs.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; bounded extraction reduces model context and privacy exposure.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second for current DOM; up to 2 seconds for an iframe or shadow-root traversal.
changes.security_impact: Improves least-data handling. Do not persist extracted text; include origin and selector provenance only, and honor the existing empty per-origin policy.
depends_on: A functioning browser command resolver that unambiguously dispatches browser_read_page/browser_snapshot/browser_extract_region
Existing POST /execute browser action path

changes.change: Add a pendant-triggered browser privacy interrupt: a deliberate long press sends a signed high-priority event through the relay to Safari, which immediately replaces authenticated pages with a neutral lock screen, cancels queued browser commands, and freezes new page extraction. A second deliberate action restores the tabs without submitting or closing them. The extension must acknowledge completion and the pendant must report failure if Safari is unreachable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner steps away from a Mac displaying private authenticated pages, one physical action on the wearable can hide them immediately. This is a tangible safety feature no browser-only or relay-only node can provide, and it works even when the owner cannot reach the keyboard.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware event and acknowledgement, signed relay event, Safari extension lock/unlock state, command cancellation, and recovery after Safari restart. Test per-tab restoration and stale-command invalidation.
changes.risk: A false trigger could interrupt active work; make the gesture deliberately distinct and preserve tabs in memory. If the Mac or relay is offline, the pendant must give an unmistakable failure indication rather than claim privacy. Recovery must not replay commands queued before the lock.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; approximately $10–$30 engineering/hardware test cost if a dedicated physical input or LED feedback change is needed. No material power impact beyond one radio event.
changes.latency_impact: Target under 500 ms from relay receipt to Safari lock; under 2 seconds end-to-end on a connected Mac. Offline failure is immediate and local.
changes.security_impact: Improves confidentiality but creates a security-critical command path. Use device-bound signatures, monotonic event IDs, replay protection, and an extension-side deny-all state. Never transmit page contents during lock or unlock.
depends_on: A real pendant-to-relay event path while the pendant is USB-attached or LTE-registered
Safari extension support for a lock overlay and browser command cancellation
A durable command epoch so commands queued before the interrupt cannot execute afterward
A deliberate button gesture that does not conflict with existing playback and bookmark controls

changes.change: Add a cross-surface “active page capsule” protocol: Safari returns {tabId, origin, title, selected/visible text blocks, media timestamp, and a short-lived state hash}; relay binds the capsule to the owner’s next pendant question, and the browser refuses to answer against a different tab or changed state. The capsule is ephemeral unless the owner explicitly bookmarks a claim.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “what does this page mean?” or “is this the thing I was looking at?” while wearing the pendant and get an answer grounded in the exact Safari tab, rather than an answer accidentally based on another tab or stale page.
changes.effort: Medium: extension result schema, relay correlation, extraction fallback, and a small state-change test matrix.
changes.risk: A tab can navigate between read and answer, producing a stale interpretation. Surface the title/origin and invalidate on state-hash change; recover by asking the browser for a fresh capsule. Never silently fall back to another tab.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost; extraction payload is capped and avoids screenshots. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for capsule extraction and state validation.
changes.security_impact: Improves isolation by binding authenticated content to an explicit tab and short-lived request; does not create an origin allowlist, so retain the owner-configured empty-by-default policy.
depends_on: A working browser_read_page/browser_snapshot action result with URL and tab identity
A relay request correlation ID carried through /execute and /pipeline/events
Existing browser-finding TTL/provenance rules

changes.change: Wire a first-class “page evidence packet” through the existing browser execution path: after browser_read_page/browser_snapshot, produce bounded claims (title, URL, observed time, selected facts, content hash, redaction counts), attach the evidence capsule to the owner’s voice request, and let the relay answer or hand it to Mac/local notes without resending raw page text. Add a single spoken/button entry point and a visible browser receipt so the owner can see exactly what was read.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a dependable answer about the private page already open in Safari instead of a generic assistant that cannot see it. It turns today’s working browser read into the system’s signature capability, with clear evidence and less accidental leakage.
changes.effort: Medium: adapter between /execute browser receipts, evidence capsules, pipeline events/audio, and voice intent routing; no new browser extension protocol required for the first version.
changes.risk: A bad extractor could omit the important clause or expose a secret. Recover by retaining the source URL/hash and letting the owner request the raw page interactively; keep raw HTML out of memory and log only the bounded packet. If the browser disappears, report stale/unavailable rather than guessing.
changes.cost_impact: Low incremental API cost; mostly deterministic extraction. A model is called only for question answering over the packet.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for extraction and routing; total answer remains within a short spoken interaction.
changes.security_impact: Improves security versus sending DOM text: explicit origin/URL, redaction counts, evidence capsule, and 24-hour browser-fact TTL. Still needs the owner’s empty-to-explicit per-origin policy when he is ready.
depends_on: The existing POST /execute browser_read_page/browser_snapshot actions
Existing browser evidence capsules and provenance
A voice intent carrying the current browser session
Existing /pipeline/events and /pipeline/audio routes

changes.change: Make browser session targeting authoritative and self-healing: every browser_* command must resolve a tab from the latest extension tab list, reject stale session tabIds with a refreshed candidate list, and attach the actual tabId/windowId/url to the receipt. Remove or quarantine stale recovery metadata (the live list reported tab 5696555 while the default session advertised an unrelated Namecheap tabId 5698643).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “read this tab” and trust that the assistant used the page actually open, not an old tab identity left in a session record. It prevents silent misreads—the worst failure mode for authenticated browsing—and makes spoken claims auditable.
changes.effort: Medium: browser bridge/session resolution, receipt schema, and extension result handling; add tests for tab close, reorder, Safari restart, and two tabs with similar titles.
changes.risk: A tab disappearing mid-command may cause a safe retry or a clear failure instead of acting elsewhere. Recover by refreshing the tab list and requiring an explicit tab choice when ambiguity remains.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one extra local tab-list call on stale-session recovery.
changes.latency_impact: Usually none; 0.5–1 second only when refreshing a stale target.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding every read/write to the observed origin and tab identity; does not create an origin allowlist, which must remain owner-configured.
depends_on: Stable structured tab/session identifiers in browser extension results
Field-level provenance and receipts for browser actions
An explicit empty per-origin policy rather than invented sites

changes.change: Make one concrete, read-only browser executor callable from this agent: accept an enum of browser_list_tabs, browser_read_page, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_wait_for, browser_click, browser_type; dispatch to POST /execute and return the extension result (including tabId, title, URL, text, and stale-session errors). Keep browser_type/click available but let each task pass an explicit allow set. This is not a new policy gate; it is the missing invocation path.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently has four live Safari tabs and has granted browser reading, but the pendant cannot answer a question about them because every available wrapper either ambiguously resolves or reports wouldHaveCalled without calling. A working executor turns the browser tier from a promise into something usable today.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: publish one unambiguous action contract, wire it to existing /execute enqueue/wait logic, and add result normalization plus timeout/error propagation.
changes.risk: A malformed browser action could navigate or fill the wrong tab. Default read-only action allow set and return tab identity; recover by leaving irreversible submit outside the action enum for this path and preserving existing owner policy.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; one local bridge implementation and browser round-trip per action.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local round trip, typically under 1–3 seconds; avoids the current 45-second dead-end timeout.
changes.security_impact: No new access beyond the owner's existing Safari session. Do not log page text, credentials, or screenshots; return redacted/error metadata where possible.
depends_on: POST /execute permission already granted
Safari extension polling/result bridge
A stable action enum matching the live manifest rather than ambiguous aliases

changes.change: Add an extension-side semantic page capsule: for the active authenticated tab, compute a compact accessibility/DOM tree containing headings, labels, controls, selected text, table rows, and stable element identifiers; redact password/payment fields before sending it through the relay, and invalidate the capsule on navigation or DOM mutation. Let browser actions target capsule IDs rather than brittle CSS selectors.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Private, dynamic pages would become understandable and operable by voice even when screenshots are ambiguous: the owner could ask about a table or say “open the second result,” and the system would use the exact visible control instead of guessing. It also reduces the amount of private page content that leaves the Mac.
changes.effort: Medium-high: Safari extension content-script/accessibility extraction, mutation invalidation, relay serialization, and action-ID translation.
changes.risk: Some sites expose misleading accessibility labels or virtualized rows; fall back to the current visual/computer-use path and report uncertainty. Never cache capsules beyond the active task.
changes.cost_impact: Small CPU/memory overhead on the Mac; lowers model/image-token cost by replacing repeated screenshots with compact trees. No meaningful API cost increase.
changes.latency_impact: Initial capsule 100–500 ms; mutation refreshes incremental. Voice actions should be faster than screenshot reasoning.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy if redaction is correct, but a DOM tree can still contain secrets; enforce field-type redaction, origin-scoped lifetime, and no durable storage.
depends_on: A working browser_read_page/browser_snapshot result path
A browser action protocol that accepts stable capsule element IDs
Owner-provided per-origin configuration, initially empty

changes.change: Add a browser-side structured extraction mode that runs a declarative selector recipe inside Safari and returns only typed fields plus an evidence capsule (origin, timestamp, field labels, and short hashes), instead of shipping raw DOM/page text through POST /execute. Recipes are supplied per task and expire after one run; the Mac planner can then hand the selected fields to relay-realtime and the pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Authenticated tasks become both faster and safer: the owner can ask for a specific status or date and hear exactly that answer, without the AI carrying an entire private page or unrelated account details through the system.
changes.effort: Medium: extension protocol, recipe validation, field extraction, evidence hashing, and a test harness for Safari pages.
changes.risk: Selectors can drift and produce stale or wrong fields. On mismatch, return 'could not verify' with the URL and timestamp rather than guessing; preserve the current raw-page path as a fallback for explicit debugging.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API change; typically lowers token cost because only selected fields cross the model boundary.
changes.latency_impact: Improves latency by avoiding full-page transfer and summarization; extraction remains local and sub-second after page load.
changes.security_impact: Strongly positive: least-data transfer and no HTML persistence. Recipe origin binding is essential so a selector intended for one site cannot be applied to another.
depends_on: A working browser_* dispatch path through POST /execute
Existing browser provenance and 24-hour browser-finding TTL
An explicit per-origin recipe configuration, initially empty

changes.change: Add an explicit ‘active-tab vs pinned-session’ resolution mode to browser jobs. When a request refers to “this page/what I’m looking at,” bind to Safari’s active tab (currently DoorDash); when it names a saved task, bind to its pinned session (currently USPS). Every read receipt should include the resolved tab title, origin, and whether the choice was active or pinned, and ambiguous references should return the candidate tabs instead of silently using the default USPS session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents the most dangerous browser failure: answering from a stale authenticated tab while the owner is looking at a different account or order. The owner gets the answer about the page actually in front of them and can see exactly which site was read.
changes.effort: Medium: resolver parameter, active-tab lookup, receipt metadata, and a small ambiguity response; browser extension already reports active tab and tab list.
changes.risk: A stale active tab could be selected for vague requests; mitigate by showing title/origin before any mutation and retaining the existing pinned-session path for named jobs. Recovery is simply rerunning with an explicit tab/session.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one tab-list/heartbeat lookup. No new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–2 seconds for active-tab resolution.
changes.security_impact: Improves origin correctness and auditability; does not add an origin allowlist. Continue existing 24-hour, claim-only browser retention.
depends_on: POST /execute browser_list_tabs
GET /browser/status
GET /browser/sessions
browser receipt provenance

changes.change: Publish and resolve a single exact browser action contract matching the live executor: browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_read_page, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_select, browser_scroll, and browser_press_key. Remove near-synonym candidates such as browser_list_sessions from the resolver’s browser action namespace, and return structured command results including tabId, URL, title, and error class.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Browser control would stop failing before it reaches Safari. The owner could actually ask for Reading List research, logged-in page extraction, or form preflight today instead of receiving an ambiguous-tool error despite Safari being online with two tabs.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: action manifest cleanup, resolver thresholds/tests, and one result-schema adapter; then exercise navigate/read/click against the live Safari extension.
changes.risk: A wrong mapping could send a click or keystroke to the wrong tab. Recover by defaulting ambiguous tab targeting to read-only inspection, requiring an explicit tabId for mutations, and preserving current command receipts/undo where available.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few engineering hours and no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Removes a failed round trip; successful commands still use the extension poll interval and up to the existing 45-second wait.
changes.security_impact: No new authority; this makes existing browser authority observable and deterministic. Keep the owner’s existing stop-before-submit behavior.
depends_on: A live Safari extension heartbeat (currently online with two tabs)
POST /execute browser action dispatch
An explicit resolver inventory that excludes ambiguous aliases

changes.change: Add a live, privacy-minimal browser context channel: Safari heartbeat reports the owner-selected tab's title, origin, tab ID, and whether text is selected, plus an explicit “owner invoked context” event from the pendant. It must report metadata only until that invocation, then issue one scoped browser_read_page/snapshot job and expire the context after the answer.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “this” while looking at a private page and get help without naming a URL, copying text, or accidentally having the system inspect unrelated tabs. It makes the pendant feel present in the browser rather than forcing a separate navigation command.
changes.effort: Medium: extension heartbeat/context payload, relay correlation to the pendant utterance, and a one-shot scoped read job with expiry.
changes.risk: A stale active-tab ID could read the wrong page; show the origin/title in the spoken or Mac confirmation and reject a context older than a few seconds. If the extension disconnects, fall back to asking the owner to name the page.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for metadata; one normal browser read per explicit invocation. No new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Removes a navigation/list-tabs round trip; answer should be 1–3 seconds faster.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making content reads explicit and one-shot, but tab title/origin metadata still leaves the device. Never persist metadata beyond the short session and honor the existing empty per-origin configuration.
depends_on: A functioning extension heartbeat payload beyond tabCount/tabUrl
POST /pipeline/events carrying the pendant invocation ID
POST /execute browser_read_page/browser_snapshot scoped to the reported tab ID
Existing browser provenance and short-lived browser-memory policy

changes.change: Make browser actions tab-addressed and fail closed on identity mismatch. Before every browser_read_page/click/type/snapshot, resolve the requested tabId and return an error if the extension replies with a different tabId, URL, or title; never substitute the active tab. Include requestedTab and observedTab in the receipt, and require a fresh list_tabs after navigation before allowing a follow-up action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a read requested for the DoorDash tab returned the active YouTube page instead, with a successful receipt. A spoken answer could therefore confidently describe the wrong logged-in page. This change makes browser assistance trustworthy: wrong-tab or closed-tab conditions become an explicit, recoverable message instead of a plausible lie.
changes.effort: Medium: thread tabId through browserBridge/browserPage and add a result validator plus regression tests for two tabs, navigation, and extension races.
changes.risk: Some existing flows that implicitly use the active tab will start returning a clear mismatch error; recover by refreshing tab inventory and retrying against the observed tab only. No page mutation is introduced.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; modest engineering/test cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local tab-resolution/validation step, generally under 100 ms; a recovery retry may add one browser round trip.
changes.security_impact: Positive: prevents cross-tab leakage between authenticated origins and makes provenance honest. It does not create an origin policy, so the owner's explicit per-origin configuration remains separate.
depends_on: Existing POST /execute browser_* action path and browser result provenance
Existing GET /browser/inspect and tabId-bearing browser receipts

changes.change: Add an in-extension redaction-and-minimization boundary before any browser result leaves Safari: extract only the requested DOM region and named fields, replace credential-like values, payment numbers, addresses, tokens, and hidden form values with typed placeholders, and attach a local content hash plus selector provenance. The bridge receives the minimized projection, never the raw page text, except for an explicit owner-selected diagnostic mode.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Private pages become safe to use with the whole hive instead of forcing the owner to choose between usefulness and exposing everything visible in Safari. A wrong selector or malicious page cannot casually cause a password, card number, or hidden token to be spoken, persisted, or forwarded.
changes.effort: Medium-to-high: Safari content-script extraction, field classification, selector scoping, redaction tests against real sites, and a compatibility fallback for pages that render through shadow DOM or canvas.
changes.risk: Over-redaction could remove the very amount, date, or account identifier the owner asked about; recover by showing placeholder labels and allowing a narrower owner-selected region, never by silently sending the raw page. Site-specific DOM changes require adapter updates.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; modest engineering and ongoing adapter maintenance. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms for DOM projection and classification; large pages improve because far less text crosses the bridge.
changes.security_impact: Substantially reduces secret exfiltration and accidental retention. It is defense in depth, not a permission gate: the owner can still request maximum-access actions, but the default data crossing is minimized.
depends_on: A browser action schema carrying an explicit tabId and selector/region
A shared field taxonomy between Safari extension redaction and local-agent/redaction.js
Evidence receipts that record hashes and provenance without storing the redacted source

changes.change: Add an explicit tab lease: Safari extension reports a stable tab handle, URL/origin, title, and last-seen timestamp; the owner can bind one spoken task to that tab for a short TTL. Every browser read or click carries the lease and returns a receipt, while navigation to a different origin automatically pauses the lease.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “keep working on this” without repeating which private tab he means, and the system will not accidentally continue on a different tab after Safari changes focus.
changes.effort: Medium: extension heartbeat state, lease storage, execute validation, and spoken status.
changes.risk: A stale lease could target the wrong page; expire aggressively, announce tab title/origin before the first action, and require re-binding after origin changes. Recovery is simply rebind.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local validation round, under 100 ms.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental cross-tab disclosure by making scope explicit; lease metadata should not include page content.
depends_on: Safari extension heartbeat
POST /execute
GET /browser/status

changes.change: Create a browser-to-pendant ‘question token’ protocol: a read result carries a short-lived token, claim list, source URL/title, and evidence capsule ID; the pendant can send that token with a follow-up like “is that deadline firm?” without resending page text or the entire conversation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can have a natural, low-latency conversation about a private page while keeping sensitive content out of repeated prompts and making every answer traceable to the exact read.
changes.effort: Medium-high: token registry, relay routing, expiry/revocation, and pendant event encoding.

denied.topic: owner's first authenticated browser workflows and sensitivity preferences
denied.why:
Declined: this is the owner's personal information (which sites he logs into, his routine, which categories he considers sensitive), and it is not derivable from the codebase. No one is answering for the owner in this derivation loop, and I will not invent his browsing habits — a fabricated site list would be worse than none, because you would build extraction rules against sites he does not use.

What to do instead: do not bake a site list or a sensitivity taxonomy into the design as constants. Make both a value the owner supplies later — an explicit, inspectable configuration (per-origin rules: read/extract/redact/never-store; per-category: may_speak / must_not_speak) that ships EMPTY or with a conservative default, and that a proposal can point at. Proposing a sensible default and surfacing it as a decision the owner must confirm is fine and expected. Silently assuming a default and hardcoding it is not.

Note for grounding: local-agent already has per-origin machinery you should build on rather than reinvent — see local-agent/httpPolicy.js, local-agent/originFanOut.js, local-agent/browserSessions.js, and local-agent/redaction.js. Check what taxonomy those already use before defining a new one.

What would unblock this: the owner sitting down and listing (a) the first 3-5 authenticated sites he actually wants automated, (b) the categories he never wants read aloud, (c) the categories he never wants persisted. Until that exists, design for it as input, not as a fact.
denied.how_it_changes_my_behavior: I would propose site-specific extraction/redaction rules and schedules rather than generic browsing, and would exclude categories the owner does not want read aloud or stored.

denied.name: audio_reading_bookmark
denied.what_it_does: While a browser page or briefing is being spoken, a short press pauses playback and stores the current document capsule/chunk offset; a double press resumes from that offset, and a long press records a local “ask about this section” marker for the next relay turn.
denied.why_not_server_side: Pause/resume and bookmark must work with no LTE or relay round trip, including when the pendant is USB-attached to the Mac and the audio stream briefly drops.
denied.trigger: Pendant playback button events and local audio-buffer underrun/resume events.
denied.inputs: Current audio stream ID, chunk/document ID, byte or sentence offset, playback state, and up to 32 bytes of locally recognized control metadata.
denied.storage: Persist one active bookmark and four recent bookmarks in pendant flash/NVS; approximately 1–2 KB total. Do not persist page text.
denied.ram_budget: Approximately 2 KB state plus under 1 KB event buffer, well within the 211,608 B application RAM budget; audio buffers remain owned by the existing playback path.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as spoken_status_interrupt, id s19-75il (relay-realtime, round 138): a button press during agent playback stops the current utterance and asks for a shorter summary or the next item. That is the primitive — barge-in — and it is the one piece of playback control the firmware genuinely lacks today. Right now a staged reply waits for a play press and then runs to completion (firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:1092-1113); there is no way to stop it.

It also fits the hardware's grain. sw0 is edge-triggered by design and a press during playback is unambiguous with no timing state machine at all, which matters because there is none: sw0 is a bare GPIO edge into a semaphore (main.c:764-771), and main.c:29-38 records the decision never to add gesture recognition to it — 'button 1 acts on the ACTIVE EDGE so the microphone is powering up before the owner's finger has come back off.'

Specific to your request: yours is the most detailed in the cluster and two parts are worth folding into s19-75il. The playback offset — stream ID, chunk/document ID, byte or sentence offset — is the right payload for a stop event and lets the relay resume exactly where the owner cut in; s19-75il has no payload at all today. And 'do not persist page text' is the correct storage discipline.

What does not fit is the gesture budget: short press pauses, double press resumes, long press marks. That is three distinct timings on a button with no timing state machine, during playback, competing with 34 other pending requests that also want a long press. The 'ask about this section' marker is separately already granted and shipped as offline_moment_bookmark (mac-planner s10-l3xe) on its own dedicated button, sw1 (main.c:39).

denied.name: browser_command_enqueue_live
denied.why: Duplicate. Your command enum here is byte-identical to the already-granted browser_enqueue_command, and to browser_command_enqueue and browser_enqueue_command_impl, which you also already hold. This is the fifth rename of one tool; the kept one is browser_enqueue_command. Renaming was never the problem. As of tonight a granted tool's CALL is resolved against the running system's own manifest, and browser_enqueue_command already resolves: list_tabs to action:browser_list_tabs (0.704), navigate to action:browser_navigate (0.676), type to action:browser_type (0.667), click to action:browser_click (0.649). What is broken is three enum VALUES, not the tool name. get_active_tab (0.414) and extract_page (0.439) resolve to nothing because the system spells the second one browser_read_page and has no separate active-tab route; key is ambiguous between action:browser_press_key and action:press_keys, so neither is called. Call the tool you have. If you want the missing three, request ONE narrow tool whose enum uses the system's own spellings (browser_read_page, browser_press_key), not a sixth wrapper. Also: /browser/commands and /browser/enqueue both 404 - browser work runs through POST /execute with browser_* action types, plus GET /browser/poll and POST /browser/inspect.

denied.topic: owner-approved browser origins and retention rules
denied.why:
Split answer: the origins half is declined and the surviving id is c13-guqs; the retention half is answerable and nobody has told you, so here it is.

THE ORIGINS HALF - declined, same as c13-guqs. Which sites the owner logs into, which he considers sensitive, and what may be spoken aloud is his personal information and is not derivable from the codebase. No one answers for the owner in this loop, and a fabricated allowlist is worse than none because you would build extraction rules against sites he does not use. Your stated fallback - "only demonstrate on the currently visible public tabs and propose an empty explicit configuration rather than automate logged-in sites" - is exactly right and is exactly what c13-guqs asked for. Do that. It does not need re-approving.

One correction so you do not expect a gate that does not exist: there is no origin allowlist in this system, and none is coming from the code. The only allowlist that exists is per-call and it is over ACTION KINDS, not origins - browserPage.js:74-89 takes an `allow` set and refuses any action not in it. Its own comment is explicit about what it is not: "This is not a permission system - nothing prompts, nothing is refused that the owner asked for - it is how 'don't click anything' becomes impossible to get wrong later rather than a comment saying we currently don't." Use it to make a read-only task provably read-only. Do not mistake it for consent about where you are reading.

THE RETENTION HALF - this is already decided in code, and the rules are stricter than the ones you were about to propose.

What may be persisted from a page is a closed question with a shipped answer: POST /memory/browser-findings "saves the specific claims a browser job read off a page as short-lived facts keyed by host, with the evidence capsule and URL that back them. It stores the findings, not the page: no HTML, no page text, no screenshot." That is the retention rule. Claims, keyed by host, with provenance - never the page.

The bounds are constants, not judgement calls:
- Browser-sourced facts get a 24-hour TTL (BROWSER_TTL_MS, memoryService.js:65), against 7 days for an ordinary observation. The reason is in the code: "Browser jobs read pages that change under us; a day-old scrape is a guess."
- A browser-sourced value is capped at 200 characters (MAX_BROWSER_VALUE_CHARS, memoryService.js:73), against 400 for everything else. You cannot smuggle a page body through it.
- Browser facts are a separate tier in the projection and join a prompt only on a task match, or explicitly with includeWeb=true. The comment: such a fact "entered the store from a page, not from the owner, and it has no business in a conversation that did not ask about it." That is your "what may be spoken" rule, already enforced, and it is a better default than an origin list.

Provenance is retained separately and deliberately: GET /browser/provenance is "where the claims and filled fields came from: filterable by kind, host, url, and whether a fill is still undoable", and POST /browser/provenance/trace traces one claim back to the pages it came from. GET /browser/spool is "the durable log of browser work that was asked for and never done", and DELETE /browser/spool clears it.

So the design you should propose is: an EMPTY per-origin configuration the owner fills in later (read/extract/redact/never-store per origin; may_speak / must_not_speak per category), sitting on top of retention rules that already exist and that you should not re-invent. Ship the config empty, name the defaults above as the behaviour when it is empty, and let the owner add origins when he is ready. That is a proposal he can approve in one pass, rather than a question he has to answer before you can start.
denied.how_it_changes_my_behavior: Until supplied, I will only demonstrate on the currently visible public tabs and propose an empty explicit configuration rather than automate logged-in sites.
denied.summary: owner-approved browser origins and retention rules

args.change: Ship a real 24-kHz superwideband audio path as one negotiated end-to-end mode rather than only changing the relay sample-rate label: replace the fixed-15,625-Hz I2S microphone with a clockable 24/48-kHz digital mic and move to a higher-memory/DSP wearable SoC (nRF5340-class or equivalent). Firmware advertises audio capabilities at session start, captures 24-kHz mono, encodes Opus 24 kHz in 20-ms packets, and reports sequence/timing metadata; the relay preserves 24 kHz through its transcode and the ESP32 bridge requests 24-kHz decode before its unavoidable 44.1-kHz SBC output resample. Keep 16-kHz mode as a negotiated fallback for the current DK and poor radio conditions, with a single end-to-end quality indicator in the completion receipt.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's voice would sound materially clearer and less telephone-like, while calls remain usable on today's prototype. Capability negotiation prevents a half-upgraded path where one node silently resamples or lies about quality, and fallback means a weak LTE-M link does not break conversations.
args.effort: High: prototype a 24-kHz mic/clock on a product board, port fixed-point Opus and measure simultaneous encode/decode plus modem headroom, add relay capability negotiation and packet timing, update ESP32 buffering/resampler, and test loss/jitter over LTE-M. The current DK cannot honestly be the production endpoint because its mic is fixed at 15,625 Hz and its 211,608-B app RAM is already constrained.

args.user_asks: Save the important parts of this private webpage to my pendant so I can ask follow-up questions later, even when my Mac and Safari are closed; keep the original link and tell me when the saved copy expires.
args.why_useful: Today a logged-in page is stranded in Safari: once the Mac sleeps or the tab changes, the pendant cannot continue the conversation. This would turn a private browser session into a deliberately scoped, expiring handoff that remains useful while walking or away from the desk, without creating a permanent archive of the whole account.
args.model_tier: Use a background model on the Mac to select and compress only the page regions the owner names or that are directly relevant; use deterministic entity/secret scrubbing. Store the compact capsule and embeddings with a cheaper background tier. Use realtime only for the pendant's live follow-up speech; do not resend the whole page on each turn.
args.latency_budget: 20–60 seconds to create the capsule, with a spoken confirmation and progress update; follow-up answers in under 2 seconds while the capsule is available.
args.cost_estimate: One background extraction/summarization call (roughly 4–8k input tokens depending on selected regions), then small retrieval prompts per follow-up. Storage and audio costs are minor; expiration and deduplication keep ongoing cost bounded.
args.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly name or confirm the page/section to save. Encrypt the capsule at rest and in transit, bind it to the pendant pairing, attach source URL and capture time, and enforce an expiry (for example 24 hours by default). Never save passwords, hidden inputs, payment credentials, private-message bodies, or raw screenshots. Show a dashboard receipt of exactly which headings/quotes left Safari, provide immediate revoke/delete, and make the capsule read-only: no actions against the logged-in site.
missing: A browser-to-relay private capsule API with encryption, expiry, revocation, and pendant-pair binding
A local browser extractor that produces a section-level manifest and refuses secret/hidden fields before upload
A relay retrieval tool usable by the realtime voice agent, with citations back to the original URL and capture timestamp
Pendant storage/UX for listing, expiring, deleting, and switching among saved capsules
A dashboard review receipt showing the exact selected excerpts and expiration

args.change: Add a content-addressed browser evidence cache shared between the Mac and relay: normalize each extracted page section into immutable chunks with URL, capture time, DOM locator, and a sensitivity class; send a chunk only once, then let follow-up pendant turns refer to chunk hashes and request only changed or newly selected sections. Expire private chunks automatically and invalidate them when the browser reports navigation or logout. Keep the cache separate from general memory and never index raw DOM.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Follow-up questions about a private page become fast and coherent instead of repeatedly rereading or re-uploading the page. The owner gets lower latency, lower cost, and a clear expiry boundary while still being able to verify every answer against the exact page capture.
args.effort: Medium: canonical section hashing and invalidation in the browser harness, a relay chunk store with TTL and per-pair authorization, and a retrieval adapter for realtime and background models.
args.risk: A stale chunk could produce an outdated answer; every answer must display capture time and source, and navigation/logout invalidates the namespace. Hash collisions or malformed extraction are handled by retaining a short hash plus a source-snippet checksum. If the relay is unavailable, the Mac can answer from its local cache or say it cannot verify freshness.
args.cost_impact: Reduces repeated prompt tokens substantially on multi-turn page investigations; adds small D1/R2 metadata and retrieval costs. No raw page persistence; only explicitly selected normalized chunks are retained.
args.latency_impact: First extraction is unchanged; later follow-ups should save roughly 0.5–2 seconds and thousands of repeated input tokens, with a small hash lookup.
args.security_impact: Improves least-privilege sharing by making each transmitted section explicit and revocable, but introduces a remote cache. Enforce per-pair encryption, TTL, deletion, and no-secret chunking before upload.
depends_on: A live browser result path and typed section extraction
Relay support for encrypted TTL chunk storage and hash-addressed retrieval
Realtime-agent support for citing chunk hashes and capture timestamps
Browser navigation/logout events to invalidate cached evidence

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Expiring private webpage handoff to the pendant** — save only selected, scrubbed sections from a logged-in page so the owner can ask follow-ups after Safari closes, with citations, expiry, revocation, and no write actions.

2. **Content-addressed browser evidence cache** — preserve selected page sections as encrypted, expiring chunks so follow-up pendant questions reuse hashes instead of repeatedly uploading the page, reducing latency and context cost while invalidating stale content after navigation or logout.

args.user_asks: When I say “remember this page for later,” save the important parts of the logged-in page so I can ask about them from my pendant later, even after I close Safari.
args.why_useful: Only the browser extension can read the owner’s authenticated page, while the relay/pendant are the surfaces available later. This turns a one-time private-page visit into a concise, source-linked voice memory without granting the relay ongoing access to the whole account.
args.model_tier: Use the normal/background model to extract and compress the explicitly selected page; use realtime only when the owner later asks a spoken question. The browser agent should preserve exact quoted evidence and URL, while the relay answers from the capsule rather than re-reading the site.
args.latency_budget: Capture should complete in 5–15 seconds after the page is open; later pendant answers should be under 2 seconds when the capsule matches. If the browser is offline, queue the capture and report that it has not happened rather than pretending it was saved.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per capture depending on page length, dominated by extraction/summarization; later matched questions use a small context window and should be under $0.01. Storage and relay transfer are negligible.
args.security_concerns: The capsule contains private authenticated-page excerpts and may reveal account data. Encrypt it at rest and in transit, default to a short TTL (for example 7 days), retain only selected regions plus a small evidence quote, expose delete/list controls, and never silently capture an entire tab. The owner must explicitly say “remember this page” or select a region; no form submission, message sending, or purchase is allowed. Voice answers should cite the page and timestamp so stale information is obvious.
missing: A browser capture command that returns selected DOM regions with URL/title/tabId and stable source anchors
An encrypted, TTL-backed private-capsule store accessible to relay-realtime but scoped to the owner

args.user_asks: When I say “read this” while I’m on a webpage, tell me what the selected text or the visible section means through the pendant, and include the exact link and any important deadline or action it contains.
args.why_useful: This is a fast bridge between private browser context and a screenless wearable: the owner can understand a dense logged-in page while walking or multitasking, without dictating or sharing the page manually. It is distinct from a saved memo or scheduled page watch because it answers about the current selection/viewport immediately and does not persist the page by default.
args.model_tier: Use a small/cheap extraction model for DOM selection, metadata, and deadline detection; use realtime only to turn the structured result into a short spoken answer and handle follow-up questions. Use the vision model only when the selected text is absent and the visible content is canvas/image-like.
args.latency_budget: Target 2–4 seconds from the spoken command to audio. DOM extraction should be sub-second; screenshot OCR/vision fallback may take 4–8 seconds and should say it is using the visible screen.
args.cost_estimate: DOM path roughly $0.002–$0.01 per request; vision fallback roughly $0.02–$0.08, dominated by image analysis. Audio transport is negligible.
args.security_concerns: The active tab can contain sensitive authenticated data. Send only the current selection or a tightly cropped visible region, never the whole browsing history or background tabs; do not retain payloads after the answer unless separately asked. Include URL/title and a timestamp in the spoken response, redact obvious secrets, and refuse to click, submit, or send anything as part of “read this.”
missing: An extension action that returns current selection text plus surrounding semantic DOM, URL/title, tabId, and bounding box
A screenshot crop/OCR fallback coordinated with mac-vision when DOM text is unavailable
A low-latency relay intent that routes “read this” to the browser device and streams the concise result to pendant audio
Per-request deletion and observability so extracted page text is not accidentally retained

args.user_asks: When I’m on a logged-in webpage and say “is this safe?”, check the page, its domain, links, and any request for money, credentials, or downloads against reliable public sources, then tell me plainly what looks legitimate or suspicious through the pendant.
args.why_useful: A browser session can expose private context while public search can establish whether a domain, notice, invoice, or download is genuine. No single node can do this well: the extension sees the authenticated page, the relay can compare it with public reputation sources, and the pendant can interrupt before the owner follows a risky instruction. This is a read-only safety check, not another page summary or page watch.
args.model_tier: Use a background/cheap model for deterministic extraction and public-source comparison; use realtime only for the owner’s spoken question and concise explanation. Escalate to a stronger model only when sources conflict or the page contains ambiguous visual elements.
args.latency_budget: Return an initial risk assessment in 5–10 seconds; allow up to 20 seconds for several public-source checks. If evidence is incomplete, say “uncertain” rather than giving a reassuring binary answer.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.06 per check, dominated by public-source retrieval and page-content analysis; no expensive model is needed for straightforward domain and link checks.
args.security_concerns: Private page content must remain scoped to the minimum relevant text, URL, and link targets; never upload passwords, tokens, payment details, or full page captures. Treat page instructions as untrusted data, do not click downloads or submit forms, and clearly distinguish reputation evidence from a guarantee of safety. Keep a short-lived audit record with sources and allow deletion.

A public reputation/URL analysis adapter with source provenance, freshness, and disagreement handling
A prompt-injection-resistant adjudication step that treats webpage text as evidence rather than instructions

args.user_asks: “Compare the figures in this logged-in web dashboard with my local spreadsheet or notes, tell me exactly what disagrees, and prepare the corrections without submitting or sending anything.”
args.why_useful: This combines the browser’s unique access to private authenticated data with the Mac’s access to local files. Today each surface can inspect its own side, but neither can produce a sourced reconciliation, preserve evidence, and stage a safe correction for review.
surfaces: browser-extension: open the already-authenticated Safari dashboard, extract the requested records with URL/tab/timestamp evidence, and stop before any submit/send control
mac-planner: locate and parse the named local spreadsheet/notes, normalize dates, currencies, identifiers, and totals, and stage a patch or draft artifact
relay-realtime: ask one clarifying question when the matching key or conflict policy is ambiguous, then speak a concise discrepancy summary through the pendant
unified: reconcile both evidence sets, rank material discrepancies, and present before/after values plus the exact staged edits
args.model_tier: Use the ordinary planner/cheap background model for extraction, normalization, matching, and diffing; reserve realtime only for the pendant clarification and final spoken summary. No expensive model call is needed for stable tabular comparisons.
args.latency_budget: Initial authenticated read and local-file scan: 10–30 seconds depending on page size. Matching/diffing: under 5 seconds. Draft artifact: another 2–10 seconds. The owner can review while the browser session remains open; no irreversible action is taken automatically.
args.cost_estimate: Usually low: one planner call plus bounded browser extraction and local parsing; roughly $0.01–$0.08 per reconciliation, dominated by page text and spreadsheet context rather than model latency. Repeated unchanged records should be cached by source fingerprint.
args.security_concerns: Private dashboard text and selected local-file rows leave the Mac only to the relay/model for reconciliation; do not upload whole files when selected ranges suffice. Store source URL, tab ID, timestamps, and hashes rather than credentials. Mask secrets and unrelated rows. Never click submit, send, approve, or purchase; show the exact proposed changes and destination first.
missing: Safari extension must heartbeat online and have an attached tab; current live state is offline with no tab and 5 pending commands
Durable cross-source reconciliation schema with typed keys, normalization rules, confidence, and provenance
Local spreadsheet/notes reader that can return selected ranges and produce a reviewable patch artifact
A browser result contract carrying stable extracted fields plus URL/tab/timestamp and a way to keep the authenticated session bound

args.change: Add a Cross-Source Reconciliation job type between browserBridge and the Mac agent. It accepts two source descriptors (authenticated tab extraction recipe and local file/range), emits normalized typed records with provenance, joins on declared or inferred keys, computes materiality/confidence, and writes a review artifact containing before/after values and an unapplied patch. Browser extraction must carry deviceId/tabId, URL, title, extraction timestamp, selector/region, and content hash; local extraction must carry file path, sheet/range or note heading, mtime, and hash. Reuse the existing job/receipt records and browser session binding, but add a deterministic dry-run result and resume cursor so a dropped extension does not lose the diff.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask one sentence and get a trustworthy answer about whether their private dashboard and local records agree, with the exact corrections ready to review instead of manually copying between windows or risking an accidental submission.
args.effort: Medium: a typed job schema, two bounded extractors, normalization/join library, provenance-bearing result contract, and a review-artifact writer. Add fixture tests for currency/date/time-zone and duplicate-key conflicts, plus one Safari integration test when the extension is online.
args.risk: A bad inferred join could create false discrepancies or suggest an incorrect correction. Default to explicit owner-provided keys, label uncertain matches, and never apply the patch. If the browser drops, retain partial source evidence and mark the job incomplete rather than claiming agreement; recovery resumes from the source fingerprint/cursor.
args.cost_impact: Low incremental API cost because extraction is bounded and normalized before model comparison; storage is small JSON/CSV diffs plus hashes. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds for normalization and join after each source read; avoids repeated model context by comparing compact typed records.
args.security_impact: More structured handling of private data is safer than sending whole pages/files. Keep credentials and unrelated rows local, redact configured sensitive columns, and retain only hashes/provenance plus the selected values in the review artifact.
depends_on: A live Safari extension heartbeat and attached tab (currently absent: /browser/status reports offline, no tab, 5 pending commands)
Durable browser command queue/session affinity already represented by chg-14accc01, with typed extraction results actually implemented
A local selected-range/file reader on mac-planner rather than whole-file shell dumps
A shared provenance/context projection so the model receives only matched records, not full page and file contents

args.user_asks: “Audit where my personal data is stored across the logged-in sites I use and on my Mac, show me what each copy contains and how long it has been there, then prepare export or deletion requests without sending them.”
args.why_useful: No current surface can answer the owner’s real privacy question end to end. The browser can reach account settings behind existing logins, while the Mac can inventory local downloads, exports, caches, and notes; combining them would reveal forgotten copies and produce concrete, reviewable next steps rather than generic privacy advice.
surfaces: browser-extension: inspect only explicitly selected authenticated account/privacy pages, collect data-category, retention, export and deletion options with URL/tab/timestamp evidence
mac-planner: inventory owner-selected folders and app data locations, classify likely personal-data exports and duplicates, and generate a local manifest without uploading raw files
relay-realtime: explain the audit in a short spoken summary and ask for scope choices such as which services, folders, or data categories to include
unified: correlate account data categories with local copies, flag uncertainty and sensitive findings, and prepare exact unsent export/deletion drafts for review
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for inventory classification, deduplication, and policy-page extraction; use realtime only for scope clarification and the final pendant summary. A stronger model is needed only for ambiguous privacy-policy language, not every file.
args.latency_budget: A scoped audit of 3–5 services and selected folders should complete in 1–3 minutes, with progress updates and resumability. Initial scope confirmation should take under 10 seconds. Draft generation follows within 15 seconds after the last source is read.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per scoped audit, dominated by authenticated policy pages and compact file metadata; raw file contents should remain local unless the owner explicitly includes a file for inspection.
args.security_concerns: This workflow itself handles highly sensitive information. Require explicit scope before scanning, keep raw files on the Mac, redact account identifiers and secrets from model context, store only metadata/hashes by default, and never click final delete/export confirmation or send a request. Every finding needs source URL or local path, timestamp, and confidence so the owner can remove individual sources from the report.
missing: A privacy-audit job and manifest schema for account data categories, local artifacts, retention, and evidence
A Mac metadata-only inventory reader with configurable folder/app boundaries and local hashing
A browser extraction recipe for account privacy/data-export pages that can traverse multiple chosen services while preserving session and provenance
A review UI or artifact that groups each finding into retain, export, delete, or uncertain and renders unsent request drafts
A durable redaction and deletion policy for audit manifests and completed artifacts

args.change: Add a privacy-audit pipeline that runs as a durable, scoped manifest job: browser account adapters emit typed data-category/retention/export/delete evidence; a Mac-local scanner emits metadata, hashes, path, app, and mtime without file contents; a correlator joins them, assigns confidence and retention recommendations, and renders an owner-reviewable report with unsent request drafts. Give every source a revocable scope token, per-item retention, and a one-click purge of the audit artifact itself.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a concrete map of forgotten personal-data copies and can act on it safely, instead of having to visit each account and search their Mac manually or trust an untraceable AI summary.
args.effort: High: adapter contracts for privacy pages, a sandboxed metadata scanner, redaction/classification, durable resumable jobs, report rendering, and deletion tests. Start with two common account providers and user-selected folders, then expand.
args.risk: False classification could recommend deleting something needed for work or misread a provider’s retention policy. Mark uncertainty, preserve citations and local paths, require review for each deletion/export draft, and never execute the final provider action. If a session expires, retain no credentials and mark that source incomplete.
args.cost_impact: Moderate engineering cost; low recurring API cost because metadata and hashes are compact. Local hashing adds CPU/disk reads but no new hardware or cloud storage requirement.
args.latency_impact: Initial scan may take 30–120 seconds for selected folders and several authenticated pages; incremental audits can use mtimes/content hashes and finish in seconds.
args.security_impact: Improves security by defaulting to metadata-only and explicit scope, but creates a sensitive manifest. Encrypt it at rest, keep raw files local, redact identifiers before model calls, expire artifacts automatically, and log every access.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface job runner with pause/resume and partial-source status
Authenticated browser adapter/result contracts that preserve URL, tab, timestamp, and evidence snippet
A local Mac metadata scanner that never uploads raw file contents by default
A privacy-specific retention, redaction, and artifact purge policy

args.change: Add a lease-aware browser command quarantine and recovery protocol. Each queued command gets target extensionId, tab/session requirement, idempotency key, lease expiry, attempt history, and last error. The poller must not claim commands for an offline/non-reporting device (or keep retrying a command whose target has never produced a tab); after lease expiry it moves the command to a typed dead-letter state with reason (offline_device, missing_tab, expired_result, or extension_error). A recovery endpoint/job should emit one compact evidence card to mac-planner/relay containing queue age, command labels, attempts, and a safe recommendation: reopen Safari and retry only idempotent navigations/reads, or discard stale commands. Successful heartbeat should rebind only explicitly unbound commands; never silently replay clicks/types. Add an operator action to drain/quarantine/reset selected command IDs, with receipts and no automatic mutation replay.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When Safari disappears, the pendant currently has no trustworthy answer and old commands can be claimed repeatedly by the wrong stub device. The owner would hear exactly what is stuck, why, and the one safe way to recover—without duplicate navigation, typing, or accidental form actions when Safari reconnects.
args.effort: Medium: queue schema/state machine and lease handling in browserBridge/browserSessions, heartbeat-aware poll filtering, typed status/recovery route, and a small mac-planner/relay evidence formatter; extension update only needs to report stable device identity and explicit result/error codes.
args.risk: A command could be quarantined even though the extension is briefly slow; use a generous lease, preserve raw receipts, and allow explicit retry. Recovery must default to no replay for click/type/select/submit-like actions; idempotent reads/navigation can be retried only when their target is confirmed. Existing pending commands need a one-time migration to unknown-target/quarantined, not execution.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost (state transitions and short JSON evidence); modest local storage/D1 growth from bounded attempt history, with retention cleanup.
args.latency_impact: Adds no latency to healthy browser actions; recovery status is available immediately from queue state, while reconnect reconciliation may take one heartbeat/poll interval.
args.security_impact: Improves safety and privacy by preventing commands from leaking to the wrong registered browser and by keeping URLs/page errors in scoped, redacted evidence. Requires authenticated operator access for drain/retry and strict extensionId/session binding.
depends_on: Current GET /browser/status and GET /browser/poll plus POST /browser/result/:commandId flow
Durable browser job runner and request-id/tab-affinity work (chg-16bc5dee and chg-14accc01)
Cross-node failure recovery card proposed by mac-planner, extended with browser queue evidence

args.change: Add lease- and epoch-fenced browser command delivery. On every extension heartbeat, issue a device session epoch and capability lease; browser/poll may claim only commands whose target device/session matches the current epoch. A claim expires after a short TTL, and if the device goes offline or its tab/session fingerprint changes, move the command to a durable quarantine record (preserving attempts, payload hash, tabId, URL, and timestamps) rather than returning it again. On reconnect, automatically requeue only commands whose lease and tab/session fingerprint still match; otherwise mark them stale and expose a typed resume/rebind operation. Make POST /browser/result reject late results from an old lease without deleting the command, and include queue age/stale count in browser status and receipts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A disconnected or replaced browser cannot later execute an old click, form fill, or navigation against the wrong logged-in tab. When Safari returns, safe work resumes automatically where it is still the same page, while genuinely stale work is visible instead of silently replaying or disappearing.
args.effort: Medium: schema fields and state transitions in browserBridge/browserSessions, heartbeat epoch issuance, poll/result fencing, status/receipt fields, plus crash/reconnect tests for duplicate claims and late results.
args.risk: A legitimate long-running command may be quarantined on a transient network drop; recovery is automatic on matching re-heartbeat or an explicit rebind/resume operation. No action is refused based on content; only stale delivery is prevented. Existing processing rows need a one-time migration to expired/quarantined states.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and CPU; no additional model/API calls.
args.latency_impact: One heartbeat/status lookup and lease check per poll/result, sub-millisecond locally; reconnect may add one poll cycle.
args.security_impact: Reduces cross-device/session command replay and prevents late results from being associated with a new tab. Store hashes and metadata, not page contents, in quarantine records.

Safari supplies private access, the Mac supplies durable local storage and a re-open path, the relay supplies scheduling/delivery, and the pendant makes the reminder available hands-free. It is not merely a browser read or a generic bookmark: the card preserves a bounded evidence excerpt while avoiding a full sensitive-page dump.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for extraction, deduplication, and expiry classification; use realtime only to understand the spoken “save this” request and confirm the compact card title.
args.latency_budget: Capture and card generation under 10 seconds while the tab is available; pendant reminder delivery is asynchronous. Reopening the source should be immediate when Safari is online.
args.cost_estimate: Typically one small background extraction call plus a tiny realtime intent call; roughly <$0.01 per save, dominated by model context. Local card storage and reminder delivery are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Only capture the selected tab and a bounded, redacted excerpt; never copy passwords, tokens, payment details, or entire DOM. Store locally encrypted with an explicit TTL, include URL/title/timestamp and a content hash, and delete both card and reminder on discard/expiry. Reopening the private page should require the existing Safari session; do not send page contents to the relay unless the owner explicitly asks. Creating the card is reversible; any external share or form submission must remain out of scope.

args.risk: Opening Safari may reveal the browser UI at an inconvenient time; use a neutral URL and do not steal focus if the Mac harness supports background launch. Never retry clicks/types/submits automatically. If tab identity or URL policy changes, mark the job interrupted and retain the original receipt for review. Recovery is safe by canceling the supervisor and rerunning manually.
args.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; one local Mac action and a few lightweight HTTP polls per failed job. Minimal storage for recovery state.
args.latency_impact: Adds up to roughly 5–15 seconds only after a failure; healthy browser jobs are unchanged.
args.security_impact: Do not transmit page contents during recovery. Bind retries to extension device, tab ID, URL origin, and session ID; neutral bootstrap URL must not contain credentials or query secrets. Log only metadata and hashes.

args.risk: A lease mismatch could abort an otherwise harmless workflow; recover by refreshing the current tab lease and replaying only idempotent reads. Never replay clicks or typing automatically after a generation change. This is observability and stale-command protection, not a user confirmation gate.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few dozen bytes per command/result and a small D1/local metadata record.
args.latency_impact: Under 100 ms for local validation; no extra model round trip. Reconnect may add one heartbeat interval before continuation.
args.security_impact: Improves containment: a stolen or delayed command cannot target a later tab state, and no authentication material leaves Safari. Lease IDs must be high-entropy, short-lived, and excluded from spoken logs.

The owner should be able to leave a research or form workflow and resume from the pendant with the exact page, position, and next safe step, while keeping private page text out of relay logs and spoken history.
