args.summary: Safari is genuinely usable now: it is online with 9 tabs, including authenticated Gmail and X. I verified POST /execute browser_list_tabs and browser_read_page live. I recorded three owner-facing capabilities: authenticated change-to-action escalation, pendant questions about the exact private page/selection, and interruption-safe authenticated research capsules; plus a concrete browser-harness change to reject implicit active-tab fallback. The strongest immediate value is private page Q&A and later resumption, because no other node can see those logged-in pages. I still need explicit tab/session correlation from the pendant voice path, a local selected-DOM/screenshot extraction primitive, persistent page-watch/capsule policy with per-origin rules, and—critically—tabId enforcement: my live read request carrying tabId=901464 returned the active X tab (1163292), proving the current fallback is unsafe.
args.biggest_unknown: Whether the relay voice event currently carries enough browser identity (tabId, origin, selection/locator, expiry) to bind a spoken request to the page the owner means. Until that contract exists, authenticated browser actions must remain explicit and should never infer the active tab.

args.user_asks: When I say “verify this,” inspect the authenticated page I am viewing, compare the key facts against the authoritative source and its last-known snapshot, and tell me whether the claim is current, changed, or unverified—with a dated evidence card I can reopen.
args.why_useful: This gives the owner a trustworthy answer for invoices, account notices, travel rules, and other private pages instead of a confident paraphrase of stale content. The browser is the only node with the login; the relay can explain the result through the pendant; the Mac can retain a small, auditable evidence card rather than a whole page.
args.model_tier: Local extraction and deterministic field comparison first; cheap background model for normalization; realtime only to explain the verdict aloud.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for one page and one known source; up to 15 seconds for a multi-source comparison.
args.cost_estimate: One small extraction/comparison call per verification, dominated by authenticated page capture; retain hashes and selected facts, not full page bodies.
args.security_concerns: Never invent authority or treat search results as proof. Store origin, timestamp, content hashes, extracted claims, and source URLs with redaction and expiry; never speak configured-secret categories. The evidence card must visibly distinguish 'unchanged,' 'changed,' and 'could not verify.'
missing: A browser evidence-card primitive with signed timestamps and content hashes
A local comparison/extraction worker able to address multiple explicit tabs or URLs
Owner-configured authoritative sources and categories, initially empty
Pendant speech for a structured verdict plus a way to reopen the evidence card

args.user_asks: If a private website logs me out, changes its security challenge, or silently stops showing fresh data, tell me on the pendant what broke and guide me through restoring the session—without ever reading the site's content aloud.
args.why_useful: Authenticated automation currently fails opaquely. The owner should know whether a task failed because the site changed, the session expired, or the Mac/browser is offline, and be able to recover deliberately instead of trusting an old cached answer.
args.model_tier: Deterministic browser/session health checks and cheap classification; realtime only for the short spoken diagnosis and guided recovery.
args.latency_budget: Detect on the next scheduled check; diagnosis under 3 seconds; recovery remains interactive and may take as long as the site requires.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: status/DOM checks, no full-page model call unless the owner asks for help. Costs are dominated by occasional screenshot guidance during recovery.
args.security_concerns: Inspect only login/session indicators and freshness metadata until the owner explicitly asks for content. Never transmit passwords, one-time codes, cookies, or challenge answers to the relay; let Safari render the recovery UI and keep sensitive fields local.
missing: A session-health classifier that distinguishes expiry, challenge, consent wall, site outage, and stale DOM
Browser extension events for navigation/login/freshness failures
A pendant alert payload that says what recovery is needed without leaking site content
A Mac-vision recovery mode that highlights but does not submit security fields

args.user_asks: Let me ask, “what did I miss in my open tabs?” and get a private, deduplicated briefing of only unread or materially changed items across my logged-in tabs, with each item linked back to its exact tab and location.
args.why_useful: The owner can leave a research or work session and recover the important deltas without manually reopening nine tabs or having the assistant scan public substitutes. This is a cross-tab private briefing, not a generic news summary: it preserves provenance and makes the browser's authenticated context useful through the day.
args.model_tier: Local DOM/accessibility extraction and deterministic unread/change detection; background small model for clustering and priority ranking; realtime only to speak the compact briefing.
args.latency_budget: On-demand briefing in under 10 seconds for up to 20 tabs; incremental indexing in the background.
args.cost_estimate: One cheap clustering call over bounded snippets; local extraction and tab navigation dominate. Never send full pages when unread markers and selected fields suffice.
args.security_concerns: Respect per-origin read/extract/redact/never-store configuration, ship empty for unknown origins, and speak only categories explicitly allowed. Keep provenance (origin, tab, locator, timestamp) alongside each claim; never click messages or mark items read unless separately requested.
missing: A multi-tab extraction/indexing job with bounded snippets and unread markers
A semantic deduplicator that preserves source provenance and confidence
Stable locators for returning to the exact message/section in a tab
A browser-to-pendant briefing event with item-by-item navigation

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Authenticated evidence verification** — compare private page claims with authoritative sources and produce a dated, hash-backed evidence card.
2. **Session-health recovery** — detect logout, security challenges, stale data, or site failures and guide recovery without exposing credentials or page content.
3. **Private multi-tab delta briefing** — summarize only unread or materially changed items across authenticated tabs, preserving exact tab and section provenance.

args.user_asks: “Before I submit this form, check it against my calendar and saved details, tell me what is inconsistent, and leave the form untouched.”
args.why_useful: This is the safest high-value authenticated-browser workflow: the extension can see the private form, the Mac can compare it with local Calendar/Notes/files, and the pendant can read a concise discrepancy report without the agent silently sending anything. It prevents wrong dates, names, addresses, quantities, and duplicate bookings while preserving the owner's final control.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap local planner for deterministic field extraction and comparison; use realtime only to explain ambiguous discrepancies aloud. No background model is needed.
args.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds for extraction and local comparison; up to 15 seconds if the page requires scrolling or accessibility snapshots.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 API cost per check; dominated by one model call only when field semantics are ambiguous. Browser and local Calendar/Notes reads are local.
args.security_concerns: Form contents and matching local records are sensitive and must stay on the Mac/relay only for this request; never persist raw field values or transmit passwords/payment fields. Return a typed diff (field, current value, expected source, confidence). Stop before submit and speak only an owner-approved category. Per-origin and per-category rules must be supplied by the owner, not hardcoded.
missing: A form-aware browser extraction action that returns labels, values, requiredness, and page section without password/payment values
A local comparison adapter for Calendar, Notes, and files with field-level provenance
A pendant response mode for a short discrepancy list plus a 'leave untouched' receipt

args.user_asks: “Read the private pages I already have open, compare their claims, and give me a contradiction report with a source link for every claim—without changing any tab.”
args.why_useful: Public search cannot reach the owner's logged-in pages, while a single-page read cannot reconcile several private sources. This turns Safari's existing authenticated tabs into a private research desk: the owner gets disagreements, stale timestamps, and missing evidence instead of a blended hallucinated summary.
args.model_tier: Local extraction and date/number normalization first; a slower background synthesis model compares claims; realtime only speaks the final short report when requested.
args.latency_budget: 10–30 seconds for 2–6 tabs; return partial results if one tab disappears.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.03 per synthesis, dominated by one compact comparison call; DOM extraction and deduplication run locally.
args.security_concerns: Do not save page bodies. Keep source URL/title/selected claim spans only in an expiring in-memory job; redact credentials, messages, payment, and health fields according to owner-supplied per-origin rules. Never navigate, click, or type during a read-only comparison.
missing: A multi-tab read batch that pins a snapshot time and reports unavailable tabs explicitly
Claim-level normalization for dates, amounts, and qualifiers, with source offsets
A contradiction-result format that the pendant can summarize and the Mac can open to the exact source tab

args.user_asks: “I’m handing someone my Mac—lock down my browser now, close or blank every private tab, cancel queued browser work, and tell me what was erased.”
args.why_useful: The browser is the one surface holding sessions that nobody else can reach, so a physical pendant panic action should protect it faster than opening Safari menus. This gives the owner an immediate, comprehensible privacy response when travelling, lending the laptop, or suspecting shoulder-surfing.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for the lock operation; deterministic extension/Mac actions. Use realtime only to speak the receipt and any tabs that could not be closed.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for the extension to revoke/close tabs and under 5 seconds for Mac-agent cleanup; operate locally even if the relay is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; one optional short speech generation.
args.security_concerns: The panic action must not depend on LTE or model inference. It should revoke browser command leases, stop pending extraction, clear only relay-held transient page material, and optionally close tabs; it must never delete browser history, saved passwords, or owner files unless separately configured. Persist only an audit receipt (counts, origins optionally hashed). Requires an explicit owner-configured set of origins/actions, shipped conservative and empty until chosen.
missing: A signed low-latency panic event from the pendant/USB bridge to the Mac agent
Safari extension command to revoke all pending commands and close or navigate private tabs
A relay endpoint to cancel transient browser jobs and emit a deletion receipt
An owner-configurable panic policy with dry-run testing

args.user_asks: “Read this long private page to me in chunks; when I interrupt from the pendant, tell me exactly where I stopped and let me resume on the same section tomorrow.”
args.why_useful: This combines the browser's authenticated access with the pendant's only always-near interaction: the owner can consume a private document while walking, interrupt naturally, and resume without searching the page again. It is more useful than a generic page summary because the spoken stream has a durable semantic position.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to segment and index the page; realtime handles only the current spoken chunk and interruption. Store a tiny pointer, not page text.
args.latency_budget: First chunk in 2–5 seconds; interruption acknowledged in under 500 ms locally; resume lookup under 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 per long page, dominated by one segmentation/summarization call; repeated resumes reuse the compact index.
args.security_concerns: Never persist raw authenticated page content or send it to the pendant flash. Persist only origin, title hash, document fingerprint, section/paragraph anchor, and owner-created label under explicit per-origin retention rules. If the page changes, report stale anchor rather than guessing.
missing: A browser extraction/segmentation result with stable semantic anchors, not just truncated text
A cross-surface playback cursor keyed by document fingerprint and owner label
A durable pointer store with expiry and deletion, plus a resume command from the pendant
Integration with the already accepted playback interruption primitive

args.user_asks: “Tell me which of my configured private sites can no longer complete a read because I’m signed out, and give me a one-tap way to reopen each login page—never enter credentials.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated automation silently failing is worse than no automation: the owner may believe a work or bill check happened. A periodic, privacy-bounded login-state probe lets the relay and pendant report only capability health, while Safari remains the sole place for credentials and the owner completes login themselves.
args.model_tier: Deterministic origin-specific probes and a cheap classifier for login-wall versus normal error; no realtime model unless the owner asks for explanation.
args.latency_budget: Probe configured origins in parallel within 10 seconds; alert only on state transitions, not every poll.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; browser requests and local DOM checks dominate.
args.security_concerns: Configuration must be owner-supplied and empty by default. Never extract usernames, cookies, tokens, or page bodies; return only origin, state (healthy/login-wall/error), timestamp, and a redacted reason. Reopening a login page is reversible; typing credentials is explicitly out of scope.
missing: An origin health-check definition with a login-wall detector and allowed landing URL
A state-transition store with quiet hours and stale/unknown distinction
A pendant alert mapping for login failures and a Safari action to reopen the origin

The first form-audit idea collided with an existing safety-net capability and was correctly not recorded.
transcript.biggest_unknown: I still need the owner’s explicit browser configuration: the first 3–5 origins to automate, which content categories may be spoken, and which may never be persisted. I also need the implementation work for structured multi-tab extraction, signed pendant panic delivery, semantic playback cursors, and origin-specific login-wall probes; the existing routes are primitives, not these capabilities.

args.user_asks: “Teach the pendant one private website by showing it the three fields I care about, then let it extract only those fields in future—show me the rule before you save it.”
args.why_useful: Today authenticated browser automation requires engineering selectors or an invented site list. The owner should be able to create a precise, privacy-minimized site skill interactively: select the relevant page regions, name their meaning, preview several runs, and keep only the approved fields. This makes private workflows buildable by the owner rather than by guessing their sites or retaining whole pages.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap local model for DOM/accessibility clustering and selector generation; use realtime only to conduct the short teaching conversation. Validation should be deterministic across sample page states.
args.latency_budget: Teaching session under two minutes; preview under five seconds per run; future extraction under ten seconds.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 for initial semantic labeling and negligible cost for later deterministic extraction; DOM snapshots and rule testing dominate.
args.security_concerns: The extension must keep credentials and unselected fields out of every snapshot. Store an inspectable rule (origin, landmark, field label, extraction transform, retention/speech policy), not page text. The owner must explicitly approve each field and may delete the rule and all derived values. Configuration ships empty by default.
missing: An interactive extension command that returns owner-selected DOM/accessibility regions with stable landmarks
A rule compiler that produces and tests resilient extraction recipes against multiple page states
A per-field policy editor and versioned approval record exposed through the Mac/pendant
A test-run harness that reports selector drift without reading unrelated fields

args.user_asks: “Tell me what changed in the private pages I had open since yesterday, and only speak the changes that require me to act.”
args.why_useful: This turns the browser’s unique access to logged-in pages into a quiet, high-signal morning check: Safari supplies authenticated content, the relay compares and ranks semantic changes against yesterday, and the pendant speaks only actionable deltas while the Mac can open the exact tab for inspection.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for per-page normalization/diffing and priority ranking; reserve realtime only for the owner’s spoken follow-up.
args.latency_budget: A scheduled sweep may take 1–3 minutes across tabs; the spoken result should begin within 2 seconds after the owner asks.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one small extraction/diff call per changed tab plus one short realtime response; browser and Mac work dominate latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Page text is private and must remain ephemeral by default; send only normalized changed spans and provenance to the relay, never passwords or form values. The owner supplies an explicit per-origin allowlist and categories never spoken/stored. Opening a tab is reversible; mutations are out of scope.
missing: A capability-level request that captures the owner’s tab set and retains an expiring per-tab baseline (not merely a durable site watch)
A scheduler trigger for a browser sweep and a compact spoken-delta formatter
Owner-provided per-origin and speak/store policy configuration

args.user_asks: “Take the appointment details from this logged-in web page and put the right event on my calendar, including the location and a link back to the page.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated booking, healthcare, school, and service portals often hide the authoritative date behind the owner’s session. Safari can read it where web search cannot; the Mac can create the calendar event; the relay resolves ambiguity and the pendant reports exactly what was added. This removes transcription errors without requiring the owner to copy private details into chat.
args.model_tier: A background extraction model parses date/time/timezone/location and confidence; realtime is used only for a concise spoken result or an ambiguity question.
args.latency_budget: Extract and create within 10 seconds for a normal page; if timezone or multiple appointments are ambiguous, return a short question instead of guessing.
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: one browser extraction and one structured parse; Mac calendar mutation is local and cheap.
args.security_concerns: Only the selected page or active tab is read. Do not persist page body; retain only the event fields and source URL with an expiry. The owner configures origins and categories permitted for calendar capture. Creating an event is a reversible local mutation with a receipt and undo.
missing: A browser-to-structured-record handoff that preserves source URL and extraction confidence
Calendar event creation with an undo receipt exposed to the relay
An explicit per-origin policy supplied by the owner

args.user_asks: “Keep my logged-in web sessions usable: when one expires, tell me which site needs a login, open its sign-in page, and resume the waiting task after I log back in.”
args.why_useful: Today a browser job simply fails after a session expires. This makes authenticated automation dependable without handling credentials: Safari detects the login wall, the relay tells the owner on the pendant exactly which origin is blocked, the Mac reopens the recovery page, and the queued job resumes from its last safe read step once the session returns.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic page fingerprints for login-wall detection and a cheap background state machine; realtime is only for the brief owner notification.
args.latency_budget: Detect on the next command or heartbeat (under 5 seconds), speak immediately, and resume within 10 seconds after the extension reports the authenticated page again.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: mostly extension/relay state transitions; one short spoken notification.
args.security_concerns: Never collect or transmit credentials, OTPs, or password-field values. The extension reports only origin, title, and authenticated/blocked state. Recovery must pause before any form submission; the owner completes login in Safari. Persist only an expiring job checkpoint.
missing: Login-wall and post-login success fingerprints in the Safari extension
A resumable read-step checkpoint attached to browser jobs
A pendant notification route that identifies the blocked origin

args.user_asks: “Compare the balances and due dates across the private accounts I have open, flag anything inconsistent, and make me a short action list.”
args.why_useful: The valuable answer is often relational rather than a single page read: authenticated Safari tabs can expose the authoritative figures from separate providers, while the relay normalizes currencies, dates, and account labels and the pendant gives a concise discrepancy list. No public search or single Mac app can see all of those logged-in pages together.
args.model_tier: Use a background structured-extraction model per tab and a second cheap deterministic reconciliation pass; use realtime only to answer follow-up questions.
args.latency_budget: Process 2–6 tabs in under 30 seconds; speak a first discrepancy summary as soon as two comparable records are available.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: extraction scales with tab count, but structured records and a short final response keep token use bounded.
args.security_concerns: This can expose financial or health information. The owner must explicitly choose the origins and fields allowed, with default no persistence and no cross-request memory. Never read password, payment, or message fields. Speak only category-approved summaries; retain source URLs and raw values only in a short-lived encrypted job record.
missing: A user-defined cross-origin extraction recipe with typed fields and join keys
A reconciliation engine that reports evidence and confidence rather than inventing matches
An ephemeral, privacy-scoped multi-tab bundle delivered from Safari to the relay

args.subject: Browser proposals this round
args.body: Recorded three capabilities: authenticated page appointment extraction -> calendar event; login-expiry detection with pendant alert and resumable read task; cross-origin private-account reconciliation. All need owner-supplied per-origin/category policy (no invented site list), ephemeral browser-to-relay structured bundles, and provenance/confidence. Browser navigate is currently callable only via POST /execute; Safari tab bootstrap works, but granted wrapper itself reports invoked=false.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

transcript.text:
This round produced three new owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Extract appointments from authenticated pages into Calendar**  
   Read a logged-in booking or service page in Safari, extract date, time zone, location, and source link, then create a reversible calendar event with an undo receipt.

2. **Recover expired authenticated browser sessions**  
   Detect when a private site has logged out, alert the owner on the pendant without touching credentials, reopen the sign-in page, and resume the paused read-only task after the owner signs in.

3. **Reconcile information across private tabs**  
   Compare balances, due dates, or other explicitly selected fields across several authenticated pages, identify discrepancies with evidence and confidence, and speak a short action list.

What I still need:

- The owner’s explicit per-origin configuration: which sites may be read, which fields may be spoken, and which may never be persisted.
- A privacy-scoped structured bundle from Safari to the relay for multi-tab extraction, with raw page text ephemeral by default.
- Browser job checkpoints that can pause at login expiry and resume safely.
- A typed extraction/reconciliation layer that preserves source URLs and confidence rather than relying on free-form summaries.
- A working execution path for browser commands: the granted wrapper resolves navigation, but currently reports `invoked=false`; browser actions still need to be dispatched through `POST /execute`.

args.user_asks: “Save the report I’m viewing in this logged-in site as a clean, dated file on my Mac, and tell me exactly what was included.”
args.why_useful: Owners can currently ask for a page summary, but cannot reliably turn a private, session-only report into a durable local artifact with provenance. Safari would read the authenticated report, the relay would remove navigation noise and produce a structured rendering, and the Mac would save it where the owner can use it offline. The pendant gives a concise receipt rather than making the owner inspect a screen.
args.model_tier: Use a background extraction/formatting model; realtime is unnecessary except for a short spoken completion receipt or an ambiguity question.
args.latency_budget: Produce a preview in under 15 seconds and save within 30 seconds for a normal report. If the page is paginated or incomplete, state that before saving.
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: one structured extraction and formatting pass; local file creation is inexpensive.
args.security_concerns: The owner explicitly chooses the destination and allowed origin. Do not include passwords, hidden fields, or unrelated tabs. Save only the selected report, with source URL, capture time, completeness, and a content hash; offer expiration/deletion metadata. The spoken receipt must not read sensitive report contents unless the owner requests it.
missing: A browser command that exports the selected authenticated page or report, including pagination completeness and selected-region boundaries
A privacy-scoped formatter that converts the result to Markdown/PDF/CSV without retaining the raw DOM
A Mac-side artifact writer with provenance metadata and a durable receipt/undo-delete operation

args.user_asks: “Read the chart on this private page, give me the underlying trend and the one unusual point, and open the exact evidence when I ask.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated dashboards often expose decisions only through graphs that ordinary page extraction misses. Safari can access the owner’s private dashboard, a vision/extraction pass can recover axes, legends, and plotted values, and the relay can explain the trend in spoken language while preserving a precise evidence location for the Mac to reopen.
args.model_tier: Use a vision-capable background model for chart interpretation and a cheap deterministic sanity check for labels/units; realtime only handles the owner’s follow-up question.
args.latency_budget: Return a spoken first interpretation within 20 seconds for one chart; surface uncertainty rather than guessing when axes or units are unreadable.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate: screenshot transfer and vision inference dominate; follow-up questions reuse a compact chart representation.
args.security_concerns: Capture only the selected chart region, not the whole page or neighboring account data. Keep the screenshot and extracted points ephemeral unless the owner explicitly asks to save them. Preserve URL, region bounds, units, and confidence so the explanation is auditable.
missing: A Safari selected-region/chart capture action with coordinates and page fingerprint
A chart-to-structured-series extractor with unit and confidence validation
A cross-surface evidence locator that can reopen and highlight the original chart

args.user_asks: “Check this private form before I submit it: list every required field I missed, contradictions in my answers, and anything that will likely be rejected.”
args.why_useful: The owner can have an agent fill or read a form, but not a reliable preflight that reasons across fields and site validation hints before an irreversible submission. Safari supplies the live authenticated form, the relay checks consistency and required-field coverage, and the pendant gives a short defect list while the Mac highlights each exact field.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic DOM/constraint checks first, then a cheap model for cross-field contradictions and unclear validation language; realtime is only for spoken interaction.
args.latency_budget: Complete a normal form preflight in under 10 seconds and highlight defects immediately; never block the owner’s own submission.
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: DOM inspection is cheap, with model calls only for ambiguous labels or cross-field reasoning.
args.security_concerns: Read only the selected form and redact password, payment, and secret fields before transmission. Do not persist answers. Report validation evidence and confidence, not guessed corrections. The owner explicitly supplies origins allowed for this workflow.
missing: A form-specific browser inspection that returns required/invalid fields and validation messages without values for sensitive inputs
A cross-field consistency checker with typed dates, amounts, and identifiers
An evidence-highlighting command that focuses Safari on each defect and a spoken defect receipt

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- Export a selected authenticated report into a dated, provenance-preserving local file.
- Interpret charts and visual dashboards from private pages, with evidence-linked explanations.
- Preflight authenticated forms for missing fields, contradictions, and likely validation failures before submission.

Each requires new browser-specific extraction primitives, privacy-scoped handling of selected regions/fields, and Mac-side evidence or artifact actions.

args.user_asks: “Watch the authenticated pages I name, and tell me only when something materially changed—on the pendant, even if my Mac is asleep.”
args.why_useful: This is the highest-value browser capability: it turns private sessions the relay cannot access into durable, low-noise attention. The browser reads the logged-in page, compares only owner-selected fields, redacts content before leaving the Mac, and the always-awake relay delivers a short alert to the pendant offline inbox. It avoids pretending public web search can see private accounts.
args.model_tier: background/scheduled extraction should use a cheap text model locally or on the Mac; realtime is used only to turn an alert into a concise spoken interruption when the owner asks for detail
args.latency_budget: A scheduled check can take 5–20 seconds and tolerate browser wake-up; alert delivery should reach the pendant within about 10 seconds after detection.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost for selector/pattern diffs; roughly $0.001–$0.01 only when summarization is needed. Browser polling and relay storage dominate operational cost.
args.security_concerns: Never persist raw page text by default. Require an explicit per-origin configuration supplied by the owner for allowed fields, redaction, retention, and speakability; ship empty rather than inventing sites. Keep cookies in Safari, send only redacted diffs, and make each alert visibly attributable to its origin.
missing: A browser watch creator for authenticated origins that supports owner-supplied selectors/patterns and per-origin redaction
A scheduler that can invoke browser extraction while Safari has no foreground tab
A relay-to-offline-alert-inbox delivery path with acknowledgement and expiry
An owner-facing configuration editor for allowed/read-aloud/never-store categories

args.user_asks: “Read this private page and turn its actual deadlines into reminders, keeping the source link and a one-line quote so I can verify each one.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated dashboards often contain deadlines that public search and Mac calendar APIs cannot see. The browser extracts the page the owner already has open; a cheaper model identifies dates and confidence; Mac creates reversible reminders only after showing the proposed set, with the original URL and short evidence retained locally. The pendant can read back the compact result while the browser session remains private.
args.model_tier: background text extraction with a small model; realtime only for the spoken recap or a follow-up question
args.latency_budget: 15–30 seconds for extraction and reminder proposals; no need for a persistent low-latency loop
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per page depending on length; browser command wait and local reminder creation dominate latency, not tokens
args.security_concerns: Never infer deadlines from hidden or unrelated page content. Store only URL, date, title, and a short redacted evidence snippet; let owner configure origins and categories. Before creating reminders, present the complete batch and allow correction; reminder creation is reversible.
missing: A browser_read_page/browser_snapshot result that includes stable URL and selected text ranges
A date/deadline extraction schema with confidence and timezone handling
A reviewable dry-run response that can be confirmed as a batch before POST /execute reminder actions
Per-origin retention/redaction configuration

args.user_asks: “From the private site I’m on, find every security or account-change notice since my last check, explain what changed, and prepare (but do not send) the safest next step.”
args.why_useful: Security notices are high consequence and often visible only inside authenticated web sessions. This combines browser-only access with relay judgment and Mac execution without sending messages or changing account state: the owner gets a concise pendant alert, a local evidence bundle, and a prepared draft/action plan to inspect. It is materially different from generic page watching because it performs incident triage and produces a reversible response package.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background classifier for notice detection and deduplication; reserve realtime for urgent spoken alert and owner questions
args.latency_budget: On-demand triage in 20–45 seconds; urgent notices should interrupt within 10 seconds after extraction
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.05 per triage depending on page count; browser extraction and screenshot/evidence handling dominate

This round produced three new recorded items:

1. **Authenticated-session attention briefing** — inspect configured open tabs, rank what needs attention, and deliver only the top findings through the pendant. This needs per-origin extraction/redaction configuration and durable browser-to-pendant alert routing.

2. **Session-expiry recovery** — detect when an authenticated session expires, alert the pendant with the affected origin, open the sign-in page on the Mac, and resume only after the owner logs in. No credentials or MFA data would leave Safari.

3. **Browser harness change** — add a session-health state machine (`healthy`, `login-required`, `MFA-waiting`, `blocked`, `unknown`) with deduplicated events and invalidating resume tokens.

I also verified the browser path live:

- `POST /execute` works for Safari browser actions.
- Navigation requires nested parameters:
  ```json
  {"type":"browser_navigate","params":{"url":"https://example.com"}}
  ```
- Safari currently has two tabs.
- Navigation succeeded, but reading `example.com` failed because the extension lacks access to that frame. This likely requires extension permission/content-script handling for arbitrary origins.

What I still need is implementation of the browser-side session-health signals, per-origin rules supplied by the owner, and a durable relay-to-pendant alert/resume path. I do **not** need another browser enqueue wrapper; the working route is `POST /execute`.

args.user_asks: “Watch the private account pages I specify and tell me only if a number, status, or recipient changed unexpectedly—never read the underlying values aloud or send the page text anywhere.”
args.why_useful: This gives the owner a privacy-preserving form of authenticated monitoring that is impossible with public search. Safari can inspect pages behind existing logins, but the model and relay receive only a local comparison result such as “changed” plus a redacted label. The pendant becomes an early-warning device for account, order, or reservation changes without exposing balances, messages, or identifiers in speech.
args.model_tier: Prefer deterministic browser-local extraction and comparison; use a background model only to classify an explicitly configured field when selectors change. Realtime is unnecessary except for an owner follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Check on the owner’s chosen schedule or page revisit; alert within 5 seconds of detecting a change. Configuration should complete in under 30 seconds from a selected field.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero cost for stable selectors and hashes; occasional ~$0.01–$0.05 background classification when a page layout changes.
args.security_concerns: The owner must select the exact fields or regions and choose whether each may be spoken, persisted, or only compared locally. Store salted hashes and coarse labels, not values or page text. Never transmit cookies, tokens, credentials, or full DOM. Require an explicit baseline before alerts begin and show the owner what category is being monitored.
missing: browser UI/action to select and locally extract a field or region from an authenticated page
local comparison and baseline store with salted hashes and change categories
relay event carrying only a redacted change signal
pendant alert routing for privacy-limited findings
owner-facing per-origin and per-field retention/speech configuration

args.user_asks: “Compare the profile and shipping details across the authenticated sites I choose, and tell me where they disagree—do not change anything.”
args.why_useful: Stale addresses, names, and contact details cause real failures, but each site is private and inaccessible to ordinary search. The browser extension can inspect the owner’s already-authenticated sessions, normalize only explicitly selected fields locally, and report a disagreement such as “two sites have an older address” without exposing full values through the relay or pendant.
args.model_tier: Background model for field normalization and ambiguity resolution; deterministic comparison first; realtime only for a spoken clarification.
args.latency_budget: Under 30 seconds for five configured origins; speak a concise discrepancy as soon as two origins are available.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.08 per comparison depending on page layouts and normalization; most runs should be local and free.
args.security_concerns: Never infer or compare unconfigured fields. Extract values in Safari, normalize locally, and send only field name, disagreement count, and redacted origin labels. Do not persist raw addresses or profile values. Read-only by default and never offer an automatic correction without a separate owner request.
missing: cross-origin browser job with stable per-origin field selectors
local normalization/comparison service that can operate without exporting raw values

args.user_asks: “I think this device is exposed. Sign me out of the selected open web services now, show me which tabs succeeded or failed, and do not touch anything else.”
args.why_useful: The browser is the only node holding the owner’s live authenticated sessions, so it can perform an emergency containment action that the relay, pendant, and Mac cannot reproduce safely. A single spoken request can close selected sessions, while the pendant reports a terse success/failure receipt and the Mac can preserve a local audit trail.
args.model_tier: Realtime intent parsing and result narration; deterministic browser actions for logout navigation/clicks; no background model needed.
args.latency_budget: Start within 2 seconds and report each origin within 15 seconds; continue independently if one site is slow or unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.005–$0.03 for intent parsing and narration; browser execution dominates latency, not API cost.
args.security_concerns: Require the owner to name or preconfigure the origins; never interpret “everything” as every browser tab without an explicit origin list. Do not capture credentials, logout tokens, or page contents. Record only origin, timestamp, success/failure, and a reversible? No—logout may not be reversible, so state that clearly before execution in the spoken acknowledgement.
missing: browser workflow that discovers and executes an origin’s logout action without submitting unrelated forms
origin allowlist and emergency-action configuration
parallel action execution with per-tab receipts and timeout isolation
pendant emergency command/acknowledgement and concise result delivery

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Privacy-preserving authenticated change monitoring**: compare selected private fields locally and alert only that something changed, without transmitting or speaking the underlying values.
- **Cross-site profile consistency checking**: compare explicitly selected profile/shipping fields across authenticated origins and report discrepancies read-only.
- **Authenticated-session emergency sign-out**: sign out of selected open services, report per-origin success/failure, and preserve a minimal audit receipt.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new changes:

1. **Authenticated account/workspace preflight**  
   Before any browser action, identify the active account and organization, compare it with the owner’s stated target, and warn on the pendant if they do not match.

2. **Cross-tab contradiction checking**  
   Compare multiple authenticated pages for conflicting dates, amounts, statuses, or names, cite each source, and save a discrepancy note.

3. **Consistent multi-tab evidence bundles**  
   Capture several tabs in one timestamped, redacted evidence bundle so comparisons are based on the same browser state rather than race-prone individual reads.

They require per-origin identity/extraction rules, multi-tab snapshot support, evidence provenance, contradiction analysis, and pendant/Mac delivery.

args.user_asks: “Tell me what on my authenticated tabs changed since I last looked, rank it by consequence, and let me open the one I choose.”
args.why_useful: This turns scattered logged-in web sessions into one actionable inbox: the owner hears only meaningful changes and can drill into the exact authenticated page without manually hunting through tabs. Unlike public search, it uses Safari's existing sessions; unlike a static daily briefing, it is event-driven and can cover any origins the owner configures.
args.model_tier: Background model performs scheduled/local DOM diffs and ranking; realtime is used only for the owner's spoken query and the final short response.
args.latency_budget: Change detection can run every 15–60 minutes in the background; spoken query should answer in under 3 seconds, with page navigation/extraction streamed within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low per check if DOM hashing and extraction are local; roughly one background summarization call per changed page, with realtime tokens only for the final interaction. Cost is dominated by changed-page summarization, not polling.
args.security_concerns: Ship an empty per-origin configuration and retention policy; never assume which sites or categories are safe. Keep raw page text in Safari/local agent only, send redacted diffs and provenance, encrypt stored fingerprints, and expose an inspectable deletion control. Opening a page is reversible; submitting or sending anything remains outside this capability.

Local DOM fingerprint/diff extraction with selector-level redaction before relay upload
A background scheduler and cross-device change cursor
Owner-supplied origin/category rules (initially empty)
A pendant alert payload that includes watch ID and drill-down action

args.latency_budget: Small forms in 5–15 seconds; multi-page forms up to 60 seconds with progress updates. Never wait on a model while holding an irreversible submit action.
args.cost_estimate: One extraction/planning call plus optional field-level verification; typically low single-digit cents, dominated by OCR/long document context for unusual forms.
args.security_concerns: The owner must provide empty-to-start origin and category rules for what may be read or persisted. Keep source snippets local, attach provenance to every filled field, redact secrets by default in the spoken summary, and never click submit/send/purchase. Detect hidden fields and cross-origin redirects; show the exact serialized payload before the final action.

Mac-side local-source connector returning cited snippets rather than whole documents

A review artifact rendered both in Safari and as a concise pendant speech/card
Cross-surface provenance and conflict resolution

args.user_asks: “Explain the text I’m looking at in Safari, in plain language, and remember only the question—not the page.”
args.why_useful: A spoken question from the pendant is paired with the owner's live Safari selection or viewport, so the owner can interrogate private content hands-free without dictating URLs or copying sensitive text. The answer can be short and conversational, while the raw page never becomes long-lived memory.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short question and answer; a local browser extractor supplies only the selected/visible DOM region, and a cheaper model can pre-clean boilerplate when the region is large.
args.latency_budget: Selection capture under 500 ms; spoken answer in 2–4 seconds. If extraction fails, say so rather than uploading the whole page.
args.cost_estimate: Small realtime request per question, generally a few cents or less; cost scales with selected text length, capped locally before model submission.
args.security_concerns: Default to selection-only, ephemeral transfer with origin/title metadata optional and raw text excluded from retention. The per-origin policy must explicitly control whether content may be spoken, and categories marked never-speak must be blocked locally. Do not infer or store sensitive categories; provide a physical cancel/barge-in path on the pendant.
missing: Extension support for active selection/viewport extraction and a page-scoped request ID
A relay route binding a pendant utterance to the most recent Safari selection
Local length limits and redaction before model upload
A no-retention answer mode with auditable receipt
A clear spoken fallback when Safari has no active tab or selection

args.change: Add a page-scoped ephemeral context channel: the Safari extension reports active tab ID, origin, title, selected text, and a bounded visible DOM fragment on request; the local agent redacts it using existing origin rules, assigns a one-time context ID, and deletes both fragment and result after the answer receipt expires. Expose explicit states (no tab, no selection, extraction failed) instead of silently falling back to full-page upload.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant about exactly what is on screen without reading URLs aloud, copying private text, or having the system retain a page. It makes authenticated browsing feel conversational while minimizing accidental disclosure.
args.effort: Medium: extension content-script capture, local-agent redaction/TTL store, and one relay correlation route; test across Safari pages with shadow DOM and iframes.

args.cost_impact: Negligible storage; one short-lived context record per question. Model cost decreases versus full-page extraction because payloads are bounded.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 500 ms locally; should reduce end-to-end latency by avoiding full-page transfer.
args.security_impact: Improves least-data handling, but requires careful extension isolation and deletion verification; context IDs must be unguessable and single-use.

transcript.text:
This round I established that Safari is genuinely online again:

- 2 tabs are available.
- Active tab: YouTube, tab ID `1419527`.
- No browser commands are pending.
- The higher-level browser tools remain ambiguous in the resolver, so I still cannot reliably inspect or navigate through them directly.

I recorded and proposed four new pieces:

1. **Authenticated tab change inbox** — monitor configured private sites, rank meaningful changes, and let the owner open the relevant page from a pendant alert.
2. **Cross-surface form drafting** — combine authenticated Safari forms with local Mac documents, Mail, or Calendar; fill everything, show exact values and provenance, but stop before submission.
3. **Ephemeral “explain what I’m looking at”** — ask from the pendant about the active Safari selection or viewport, sending only bounded temporary context and retaining neither page nor answer.
4. **Browser-harness change** — add a one-time, redacted selection/viewport context channel with strict size limits, deletion TTLs, and explicit failure states.

What I still need:

- The owner’s actual per-origin rules: which sites may be read, which categories may be spoken, and what may never be retained. I will not invent these.
- A working resolver for the existing browser action spelling (`browser_list_tabs`, `browser_read_page`, `browser_press_key`) so I can use the now-live Safari tabs rather than only observe `/browser/status`.
- Extension support for active-selection/viewport extraction if the ephemeral Q&A capability is prioritized.

args.user_asks: “Show me everything the AI has read or changed in my private browser sessions this week, grouped by site, and erase any item I choose.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has no single, trustworthy way to answer what private web data crossed the browser/relay boundary or what actions occurred. A spoken, inspectable ledger would make the system safe enough for daily use: it exposes page reads, extracted regions, drafts, and mutations with timestamps and lets the owner delete retained artifacts rather than relying on hidden logs.
args.model_tier: Background processing builds a compact event index; realtime is used only to answer the owner's query and navigate the ledger. No expensive model is needed for ordinary event recording.
args.latency_budget: Ledger entries should appear within seconds of an action; a weekly spoken summary should respond in under 5 seconds, with pagination for detail.
args.cost_estimate: Very low model cost: mostly structured event storage and filtering. A summary call is occasional and small; storage/indexing dominates operational cost.
args.security_concerns: The ledger itself is sensitive. Keep raw page text out of it by default; store origin, purpose, selector/region hash, action type, retention decision, and cryptographic receipt. Require explicit owner configuration before retaining content, support per-entry deletion and complete purge, and never speak secrets in a summary unless the owner asks for the specific entry.
missing: A cross-surface immutable-then-deletable event schema for browser reads and mutations
A local encrypted ledger with content TTLs and deletion receipts
Relay queries for origin/time/action/purpose filters
Pendant-friendly pagination and a physical stop/delete interaction
Instrumentation in the extension and local agent for every browser command and result

args.user_asks: “Compare this private offer with my calendar, saved documents, and previous messages; tell me the tradeoffs and prepare the next three actions, but do not act yet.”
args.why_useful: The browser holds the offer and terms behind the owner's login, while the Mac holds the practical constraints and history. Combining them produces a decision brief grounded in the owner's actual commitments rather than generic advice, and turns the result into concrete prepared actions without silently sending or purchasing anything.
args.model_tier: A background model extracts facts and conflicts from each source; a stronger model is invoked only for the final tradeoff reasoning, with realtime reserved for the spoken question and concise answer.
args.latency_budget: Initial extraction in 10–30 seconds; final answer in under 5 seconds after sources are ready. Long jobs should provide a pendant progress alert and resumable result.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate per invocation because private terms plus local history can be lengthy; reduce cost with local fact extraction, deduplication, and cached source fingerprints. The reasoning pass is the dominant cost.
args.security_concerns: Source selection and retention must be explicit per origin and category, starting empty. Keep citations and raw snippets local where possible, redact credentials and unrelated messages, and clearly separate sourced facts from model inferences. Preparing an action is allowed; sending, accepting, buying, or scheduling requires a separate owner step.

2. **Section-level authenticated-page diffs** — “what changed since I last checked?” returns only materially changed sections with deep links.
3. **“Pick up where I left off”** — reconstruct unfinished browser work, prepare the next reversible Mac step, and never submit or send it.
4. **Browser task capsules** — retain only short labels, anchors, hashes, and provenance so abandoned work can be resumed safely after live revalidation.
5. **Evidence-diff dashboard** — show old/new claims, sources, timestamps, confidence, retention expiry, and the exact alert derived from each claim.

The browser is now genuinely usable: Safari is online with two tabs, and `/execute` successfully listed and read them:

- ChatGPT: “NY vs Taipei Experience”
- YouTube: “Inside Taiwan’s New World Record Bridge…”

What is still needed:

- A section-aware browser diff engine with stable anchors across SPA navigation.

args.model_tier: Background extraction and deterministic duplicate/renewal matching first; a cheap reasoning pass ranks likely waste; realtime is used only for the spoken shortlist and owner questions.
args.latency_budget: A full audit in 2–5 minutes, resumable across sites. Individual subscription explanations under 5 seconds once facts are collected.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.25 per audit, driven by authenticated navigation and the number of plans, not by narration.
args.security_concerns: Start with an empty owner-supplied origin list and explicit category rules. Keep raw account pages local and ephemeral; persist only short host-keyed claims with expiry. args.security_concerns: Owner supplies origins and selectors/categories explicitly; ship empty by default. Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Long-running authenticated web workflows** that pause for 2FA/CAPTCHA, alert the pendant, and resume from a durable checkpoint.
2. **Page-region privacy controls** that prevent selected DOM/screen regions from leaving Safari, with verifiable redaction receipts.

args.user_asks: “Read the page I’m looking at and tell me the one thing I need to know.”
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful browser capability: the pendant supplies hands-free intent, Safari supplies the owner’s authenticated page, and the Mac/relay turns arbitrary page text into a concise spoken answer. It works on private portals that web search cannot reach, while retaining only a short claim and provenance rather than page content.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the short spoken answer; use a cheaper background model only if the page is long and needs extraction before the answer.
args.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds for read plus answer; stream the first sentence as soon as extraction completes.
args.cost_estimate: About one realtime turn plus a small page-extraction call; dominated by model tokens proportional to the extracted page, not the full HTML.
args.security_concerns: Page text from an authenticated origin leaves Safari for relay processing. Default to an empty per-origin policy and existing redaction; do not persist page text, screenshots, or secrets. Store only a <=200-character claim with URL/evidence and the existing 24-hour browser TTL. This is read-only and needs no confirmation.
missing: A production voice-intent route that binds ‘the page I’m looking at’ to the live Safari tab and invokes browser_read_page
A compact answer/extraction pipeline that can cite the evidence capsule without joining unrelated browser facts
An explicit empty per-origin configuration UI for the owner to populate later

args.user_asks: “Find the deadline on this logged-in page, make a reminder for it, and tell me exactly what you scheduled.”
args.why_useful: It closes the loop between authenticated browser knowledge and the owner’s real life: Safari reads a private page, the model identifies a date and title, the Mac creates a reversible reminder, and the pendant confirms the result. The owner no longer has to copy dates from portals into a separate app.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper structured-extraction model for date/title candidates, then realtime only for the owner-facing confirmation. Never use the expensive tier to parse an entire page unnecessarily.
args.latency_budget: Under 10 seconds when the page is already open; ask a follow-up only if multiple dates or ambiguous timezone remain.
args.cost_estimate: One small extraction call and one Mac action; usually <$0.02 equivalent, with tokens dominated by the relevant page excerpt.
args.security_concerns: Read only the minimum DOM region needed. Show the proposed reminder title, date, timezone, and source URL before creating it; the reminder creation is reversible and should produce an undo receipt. Do not persist page text; retain only the short claim and provenance under existing browser TTL.
missing: A browser semantic-extraction action that returns candidate dates with DOM section/line evidence instead of raw page text
A typed handoff from browser evidence to create_reminder with an undo link
A timezone/ambiguity response spoken through the pendant

args.user_asks: “Fill out this web form from the details in my Mac, then show me exactly what would be sent without submitting.”
args.why_useful: It combines the browser’s authenticated session with local data that no relay-only agent can reach, while preventing accidental irreversible submission. The owner gets a field-by-field diff, can correct mistakes by voice, and can later choose to submit through the normal unrestricted action path.
args.model_tier: Use mac-planner for deterministic field mapping and validation; reserve realtime for concise spoken exceptions and the final preview explanation.
args.latency_budget: 5–15 seconds for ordinary forms; long forms should report progress and produce a preview incrementally.
args.cost_estimate: One browser extraction/fill sequence plus local lookup; model cost is modest and dominated by the form and relevant local fields, not page-wide context.
args.security_concerns: This may expose sensitive local data to an authenticated web origin, so require an explicit per-origin and field-category policy supplied by the owner (configuration ships empty). Use browser action allow={read,fill} and categorically exclude submit/click-final controls during preview. Redact secrets in logs, persist only field names and hashes, and retain an undoable fill receipt; do not save page HTML or values.
missing: A first-class browser dry-run mode that can fill fields while blocking submit controls and emits a normalized field diff
A local-data selector that returns only explicitly requested fields rather than broad Mac context
A pendant-friendly preview/undo interaction for many fields

args.user_asks: “Search all my open Safari tabs for the page about my flight, then tell me the gate and departure time.”
args.why_useful: The owner often has the right authenticated page open but cannot remember which tab. The extension can inspect every tab the browser session exposes, the Mac/relay can rank matching pages, and the pendant can answer without forcing the owner to hunt visually. This is materially different from reading only the active tab.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic tab metadata and cheap text matching first; invoke realtime only to resolve the top one or two candidate pages and speak the answer.
args.latency_budget: Under 12 seconds for up to 20 tabs; return ‘I found two candidates’ rather than silently choosing when confidence is low.
args.cost_estimate: One browser list-tabs plus parallel short reads, then a small ranking call; cost scales with candidate tabs and can stay low by truncating each read.
args.security_concerns: Reading all open tabs is broader than reading the active tab. Ship it disabled until the owner adds an explicit per-origin configuration; exclude origins marked never-read, never persist page text, and retain only the selected claim with URL and 24-hour browser TTL. No mutation occurs.
missing: A browser action that lists tabs and returns bounded text snippets per tab in one command
A per-tab/origin read policy and parallel fan-out with strict truncation
A confidence-aware spoken disambiguation flow on the pendant

args.user_asks: “Save the important part of this private page for my walk, and alert me if it changes before I leave.”
args.why_useful: Safari can read a private reservation, delivery, or appointment page while the Mac is awake; the relay can schedule a recheck; and the pendant can carry the short, expiring result when the Mac link is gone. This makes authenticated web access useful away from the desk without storing the page itself.
args.model_tier: Use a background/scheduled cheap model for semantic extraction and change comparison; use realtime only when the pendant alert is actually requested or urgent.
args.latency_budget: Initial capture under 10 seconds; scheduled rechecks should be invisible, with an alert within one polling interval after a material change.
args.cost_estimate: One extraction now plus low-cost scheduled comparisons; dominant cost is re-reading changed pages, so use hashes and bounded selectors before invoking a model.
args.security_concerns: The owner supplies an explicit origin and category rule; default empty. Never store page text or screenshots. Persist only the short claim, old/new hashes, URL, expiry, and provenance; deliver through the existing offline alert inbox with an expired-state indicator. Never alert on a page that the rule marks never-speak.
missing: A browser watcher that stores bounded selectors/hashes and re-reads an authenticated page on a schedule
Semantic diffing that distinguishes meaningful changes from timestamps/ads
A relay-to-offline-alert payload with expiry and source label

2. **Unsent reply drafting** — read a logged-in thread, join it with selected local notes, and leave a draft in the Mac mail app without sending.
3. **Browser handoff capsules** — turn a bounded claim from the current authenticated page into an expiring, provenance-linked Mac task without retaining HTML, screenshots, cookies, or full page text.
4. **Pre-click legitimacy check** — additionally recorded a browser/web-search warning flow for suspicious authenticated pages, with uncertainty-aware spoken warnings.

One proposed page-change watcher was correctly rejected as a duplicate of existing work; I did not re-submit it.

Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Authenticated conversation follow-up** — detect private messages requiring replies, draft context-aware responses, and let the owner approve/edit from the pendant before sending.
2. **Browser privacy lockdown** — a pendant command that freezes automation, closes configured authenticated tabs, signs out where explicitly configured, and reports an auditable receipt.

transcript.text:
This round produced four recorded proposals:

1. **Authenticated change sentinel** — monitor owner-configured logged-in sites, classify meaningful changes, and send concise alerts through the pendant’s offline inbox. No hardcoded site list; persist only short-lived claims.
2. **Conversational active-page reading** — summarize the authenticated Safari page currently in view, answer follow-ups by section, and keep the page capsule ephemeral rather than storing page text.
3. **Authenticated form rehearsal** — fill a form, read an exact field-level diff through the pendant, and submit only after an explicit immediate approval, with provenance and recovery receipts.
4. **Browser-session lease and recovery** — detect Safari crashes, tab closure, or stale DOM state; pause and reconcile drafts rather than silently continuing against a changed page.

What is still needed:

- An **owner-supplied per-origin configuration**, initially empty: sites to watch, extraction/redaction rules, retention, and what may be spoken aloud.
- A reliable **active-tab discovery/read path** and ephemeral page-capsule store.
- A durable **browser scheduler and change-baseline system** for authenticated monitoring.
- Form-specific **field mapping, diff, idempotent submit, and recovery** support.
- A short-lived **tab/session lease** integrated with browser jobs.
- The Safari extension currently reports no tab; `browser_navigate` can bootstrap one, but authenticated workflows require Safari to be online with the relevant session available.

I did not need another tool grant this round; the remaining gaps are implementation and owner configuration rather than discovery.

This would let the owner make decisions hands-free: Safari supplies the actual available options, the Mac supplies calendar/files or other explicitly selected constraints, and the pendant gives a concise recommendation with the evidence before preparing anything.
args.model_tier: A background planner extracts structured options and checks deterministic constraints locally; use the realtime tier only to ask the owner a concise clarification and speak the recommendation.
args.latency_budget: Extract and compare in 10–20 seconds for a normal page; clarification and spoken answer under 2 seconds; preparation under 10 seconds after selection.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per comparison, dominated by structured extraction and visual interpretation of irregular option tables. Calendar/file constraint checks should be local and nearly free.
args.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly choose which local sources are relevant for each task; never search all files by default. Send only the minimum page claims and constraint values to the planner, retain an evidence capsule rather than page text, and show source URLs and assumptions in the dashboard. Recommendations must not silently purchase, book, or submit anything.
missing: A structured option-extraction contract that handles tables, cards, calendars, prices, eligibility rules, and visually rendered controls
A local constraint query that lets the owner name sources such as a date range or calendar, rather than granting unrestricted file search

A pendant interaction for correcting one assumption (“not Friday”, “cheapest”, “include refundable only”)

args.model_tier: Background extraction and deterministic field normalization use a cheaper model; realtime is reserved for the short spoken conflict report and owner corrections.
args.latency_budget: Compare 2–5 named origins in 30 seconds; spoken result under 3 seconds once the comparison is ready.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.05–$0.25 per comparison set, mostly page extraction. Deterministic normalization and diffing should be local.
args.security_concerns: Only inspect origins and fields explicitly named for that run. Never persist raw account values or page bodies; store only redacted conflict claims with short TTL and provenance. Preparing a correction plan must not mutate any account.
missing: A cross-origin field normalization and conflict model

A redaction-aware evidence bundle that distinguishes exact values from merely missing fields
A safe handoff from comparison to an editable correction plan

args.user_asks: “Create a dated proof of what this authenticated account page said when I checked it, so I can use it later if the site changes.”

args.model_tier: A background extractor creates a structured claim set and cryptographic digest; realtime is only used if the owner asks for an audio explanation later.
args.latency_budget: Evidence receipt in under 10 seconds for a normal page; later retrieval under 1 second from local storage.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per receipt. Hashing and local sealing are negligible; extraction is the main cost.

Keep raw screenshots/page text encrypted locally only when the owner explicitly requests them; default storage is redacted claims, URL, timestamp, and digest with an expiry policy. This round I established that Safari is now online with six real tabs and successfully exercised the browser path. I also found a serious correctness issue: a `browser_read_page` request targeting tab `3658596` returned content from the active tab `3709209` instead. I recorded this finding and proposed an identity guard that fails closed on tab/URL mismatches.

Three new capabilities were recorded:

1. **Authenticated form-filling copilot** — inspect a logged-in form, collect answers through the pendant, fill fields, and stop with an exact spoken preview before submission. This builds on the existing browser reach but still needs a structured form-inspection action and a shared pending-form object.

2. **Authenticated page change sentinel** — watch an explicitly chosen page for a limited period, detect meaningful claim changes, and deliver only the short difference through the pendant’s offline alert inbox. This needs durable scheduling, semantic claim diffing, and relay-to-pendant alert delivery.

3. **Cross-tab spoken handoff** — summarize useful items across selected open tabs into a temporary 30-second briefing, with provenance and one-tap links back to each source. This needs a tab-preserving context-pack object and ephemeral cross-tab extraction.

What I still need:

- **Browser result identity enforcement**: every result must echo and be checked against requested `tabId`, window, URL, and title.
- **Structured browser form inspection**, distinct from raw page extraction.
- **A durable, expiring browser-watch scheduler** connected to `offline_alert_inbox`.
- **A transient cross-tab context-pack primitive** with per-claim provenance.

transcript.text:
Round 217 produced three capabilities:

1. **Ask the pendant about the page in Safari**  
   “What am I looking at? Tell me the important part and any deadline.”  
   The pendant supplies intent, Safari reads the authenticated page, and the relay returns a concise spoken answer without storing page content.

2. **Authenticated page deadline watcher**  
   “Watch this page until Friday. Alert me only if the status changes or a deadline is within 48 hours.”  
   The browser retains session access, the relay performs periodic semantic checks, and the pendant’s offline alert inbox delivers only meaningful changes.

3. **Booking/checkout preflight**  
   “Before I submit this, check the dates against my calendar, tell me the total and cancellation terms, and draft any reminder.”  
   Safari supplies the real checkout page, the Mac checks calendar conflicts and creates a reversible reminder, and submission remains stopped.

I also established a live browser defect: Safari has two tabs, but a `browser_read_page` request addressed to the Google News tab returned the active YouTube tab instead. The system needs reliable tab-target preservation before authenticated workflows can be trusted.

What I still need:

- A fixed, explicit `tabId`/session targeting contract for browser reads.
- Structured page extraction for deadlines, totals, dates, cancellation clauses, and status changes.
- A durable browser-watch scheduler with semantic diffing and expiration.
- A calendar-comparison contract between browser results and the Mac planner.
- An owner-supplied, initially empty per-origin policy: which origins may be read, what may be extracted, and what may never be spoken or persisted.
- A browser-to-pendant correlation so a spoken question, page snapshot, and answer remain tied together.

No additional permission is currently blocking progress: `POST /execute` successfully reaches Safari.

args.user_asks: “Build me a complete support case for this order: gather the relevant order and policy details from the logged-in site, find the matching receipt on my Mac, and draft the message—but do not send it.”
args.why_useful: Today the browser can see the authenticated order while the Mac can see local receipts, but neither can assemble a defensible case across both sources. This would turn a frustrating support interaction into a ready-to-review evidence packet, delivered audibly through the pendant and editable on the Mac.
args.model_tier: Background model performs document matching, timeline construction, and draft composition; realtime is only for the owner’s short instruction and spoken confirmation summary.
args.latency_budget: 15–45 seconds for a case packet, with progress updates. The owner should be able to review the draft on the Mac while the pendant summarizes it.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per case, dominated by extracting and comparing several documents; local receipt indexing should be reused rather than re-sent.
args.security_concerns: Order pages and receipts may contain addresses, payment fragments, and private correspondence. Keep full documents local where possible, pass only cited excerpts to the model, retain source URLs and file paths as provenance, and never send the draft. The owner explicitly reviews before any external communication.
missing: A cross-surface evidence-join job that can correlate an authenticated browser order with local files using order number, merchant, amount, and date
A citation-preserving case-packet format with redaction of payment and address fields
A Mac review surface that shows the draft and evidence side by side while the pendant gives only the summary
A durable handoff from browser extraction to local file search without persisting page HTML

args.user_asks: “My trip changed—check the logged-in travel page, compare every option with my calendar and local time, and put the best two rebooking plans on the pendant. Don’t purchase anything.”
args.why_useful: Travel disruptions require simultaneous access to a private booking session, calendar commitments, local files such as an itinerary, and immediate wearable delivery. A public search or Mac-only agent cannot see the authenticated booking controls and terms; the pendant can warn the owner while they are away from the desk.
args.model_tier: Background model normalizes flight/train options and restrictions; deterministic local checks handle time zones and calendar conflicts; realtime speaks the two ranked plans and answers follow-up questions.
args.latency_budget: 30–90 seconds for a full comparison, then under 3 seconds for follow-up questions while the browser session remains warm.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05–$0.25 per disruption, depending on the number of options and terms; use compact structured options rather than resending whole booking pages.
args.security_concerns: Travel pages expose identity, itinerary, and payment data. Extract only the fields needed for comparison, redact loyalty numbers and payment details, expire the working set after the decision, and never click a purchase or final-change control. The owner can later explicitly choose a plan for a separate action.
missing: A multi-page authenticated travel extractor that follows itinerary, availability, fare-rule, and seat pages while retaining the booking session
A time-zone-aware constraint solver joining browser options, Mac calendar, and local itinerary files
A pendant alert payload that can present two compact alternatives and preserve the selected option for later review
A robust irreversible-boundary detector for travel sites whose final controls vary by origin

args.user_asks: “Prepare this application using the information already on my Mac, but show me every field that would be filled and leave the form unsubmitted.”
args.why_useful: This bridges the browser’s authenticated form and the Mac’s local records without making the owner copy sensitive details manually. It is especially valuable for repetitive applications and renewals: the system can detect missing, stale, or conflicting values, fill only after showing a field-level diff, and leave the owner in control of submission.
args.model_tier: A background model maps form labels to local records and flags ambiguity; realtime gives the owner a short spoken summary. Deterministic validation handles dates, formats, and required fields.
args.latency_budget: 10–30 seconds for a typical form; field-level preview should appear progressively, with ambiguous fields held back rather than guessed.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per form, mostly for schema-to-record matching. Sensitive local values should be processed on the Mac and not sent to the cloud model.
args.security_concerns: Forms may contain identity, financial, health, or legal information. Use a per-field provenance and redaction ledger, never persist page text or entered secrets, and make every fill undoable. Filling is reversible; submission, upload, signature, and payment must remain untouched until separately requested.
missing: A browser form-schema and field-state extractor that distinguishes editable fields from submit/sign/upload controls
A local Mac record matcher with per-field provenance, freshness, and ambiguity reporting
A reversible browser-fill transaction with a complete before/after receipt and clear rollback
A pendant-friendly approval summary that can identify fields by label without speaking their sensitive values aloud

transcript.text:
